caveats: Non-ACTIVE coverage is not applicable to this check and needs separate active-status review. A missing timestamp with PENDING_INITIAL_SCAN, PENDING_REVIVAL_SCAN or SCAN_IN_PROGRESS is not applicable. Inspector2 has no universal safe force-scan operation for every covered resource type.

caveats: The age is based on first observation, not last update or severity. A finding can remain active despite a deployment until Inspector rescans; there is no universal safe fix API for heterogeneous vulnerabilities.

steps: List ACTIVE findings and compare each firstObservedAt with the snapshot capture time to identify those older than 192 days.

aws.cb.inspector2.findings_within_max_ag.summary: An enabled Inspector2 Region fails when any active finding firstObservedAt is more than 192 days before capture time, indicating overdue triage.

aws.cb.inspector2.kev_findings_within_du.summary: An enabled Inspector2 Region fails when an active CISA KEV finding has cisaData.dateDue earlier than capture time, indicating a missed remediation deadline.

aws.cb.inspector2.no_active_findings.summary: An enabled Inspector2 Region fails while its active finding inventory is nonempty, indicating at least one unresolved detected issue.

caveats: A finding whose detail response was not collected is UNKNOWN, not proof that it is outside CISA KEV. There is no universal safe patch command for all resource types; suppression without a substantiated false-positive review hides a known exploited issue.

caveats: Existing-domain encryption requires OpenSearch or Elasticsearch 6.7 or later and cannot be enabled while UltraWarm or cold storage is enabled; older domains need an owner-planned upgrade or replacement. aws.cb.opensearch.encryption_at_rest.summary: OpenSearch domain EncryptionAtRestOptions.Enabled is false, leaving its indexed data outside the at-rest encryption setting checked here.

caveats: Backtrack is supported only for reviewed Aurora MySQL versions and Regions; other engines or documented unsupported versions/Regions are NOT_APPLICABLE, while unrecognized version or Region and missing/denied window evidence are UNKNOWN.

BacktrackWindow=0 is disabled and fails this predicate. AWS does not support enabling Backtrack on an existing cluster when it was absent at creation; do not prescribe an in-place ModifyDBCluster activation. Backtrack is not a backup replacement and can add charges.

cli.label: Inspect identified Aurora MySQL cluster, engine version and Backtrack window

iac.code: For an owner-reviewed replacement or snapshot-restored Aurora MySQL cluster in a supported Region and version, declare a positive Backtrack window at creation, then plan capacity, recovery testing, endpoint cutover and cost review; do not claim in-place activation on an existing disabled cluster.
iac.label: Review Aurora MySQL cluster replacement declaration

steps: Inspect the exact DBClusterArn, Engine, EngineVersion and BacktrackWindow in its Region; confirm that the reviewed Aurora MySQL version and Region support Backtrack.

If the observed BacktrackWindow is zero, review recovery objectives, existing backups, costs, client endpoints and dependencies with the database owner; a missing or malformed window is unresolved evidence, not a disabled finding.

For an existing disabled cluster, plan a separately approved new or snapshot-restored Aurora MySQL cluster with a positive Backtrack window at creation, test the replacement and client cutover, then verify the observed positive window before retiring the old cluster.
aws.cb.rds.aurora_backtracking_configure.summary: A supported Aurora MySQL DB cluster has BacktrackWindow=0, so the configured Backtrack feature is disabled.

caveats: The source checks a protected-resource record, which AWS can retain regardless of recovery point status. It does not prove the latest point is valid or restorable; non-Aurora engines are not applicable.

iac.code: Declare DBClusterArn in an owner-approved backup_plan selection, exact Resources or verified tag ListOfTags condition, with vault/retention/KMS and completed backup and restore evidence.

Have the database and backup owners approve a specific plan, resource selection or tag condition, backup vault, retention, KMS key and recovery objective; verify any existing backup path.
Create the reviewed selection, let a scheduled backup complete, then verify a matching protected-resource record and test restore into an isolated environment.
aws.cb.rds.aurora_cluster_protected_reso.summary: An Aurora cluster ARN has no AWS Backup protected resource record with ResourceType Aurora.

caveats: The upstream label says DB cluster, but this native evaluator reads rds_instance rows; Aurora engine upgrades are cluster operations. A nonmatching EngineVersion is not proof of current patching. Major upgrades may require application changes and downtime.

Have the database owner select a currently supported compatible engine target, test extensions and clients, confirm backups and rehearse a restore or blue/green rollback.
Upgrade the owning Aurora cluster and verify every member instance version after cutover.
aws.cb.rds.aurora_postgres_local_file_re.summary: A Aurora PostgreSQL DB instance EngineVersion exactly matches 10.11, 10.12, 10.13, 11.6, 11.7 or 11.8, versions flagged by the pinned database-version rule.

aws.cb.rds.aurora_postgres_postgresql_lo.summary: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster lacks postgresql in EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports, so its database log is not declared for CloudWatch export.

caveats: This check includes every engine and truncates the day component of the expiry delta; a certificate close to eight days can enter the seven-day band. Missing certificate join is UNKNOWN, not proof of expiry. Some engine versions support rotation without restart while others need a restart; do not assume either behavior without checking the instance capabilities.

Have database, PKI and application owners select a supported newer CA, distribute client trust anchors first, and plan the maintenance/reboot behavior and rollback.
Modify the instance to the reviewed CA after client readiness, then test TLS verification and recheck the joined certificate expiry.
aws.cb.rds.ca_certificate_not_expiring_7.summary: An RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill has seven or fewer truncated days remaining at capture.

caveats: DocumentDB is not applicable. The source joins CACertificateIdentifier to one collected rds_certificate and returns UNKNOWN if unresolved; exactly three calendar months remaining still fails. Client trust stores must be updated before rotation. Some engine versions support rotation without restart while others need a restart; do not assume either behavior without checking the instance capabilities.

aws.cb.rds.ca_certificate_valid_3_months.summary: A non-DocumentDB RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill is no later than three calendar months after capture.
