iac.label: Review RDS db-security-group event subscription

steps: Inspect all rds_instance resources, existing RDS event subscriptions with SourceType=db-security-group, Enabled, EventCategoriesList and SourceIds scope.
Have database and operations owners approve an SNS topic, delivery permissions, recipient/on-call routing and the failure, configuration change categories or all categories.
Create the complete reviewed subscription, verify Enabled and event delivery to the monitored recipient, and check that SourceIds cover the intended resources.
aws.cb.rds.security_group_critical_event.summary: A Region with rds instance resources has no enabled db-security-group event subscription covering failure, configuration change.

caveats: Only the sqlserver-ee engine family is applicable. This check compares declared types, not actual delivery, useful logging parameters or CloudWatch retention.

cli.label: Apply reviewed RDS instance log exports

iac.code: For DBInstanceArn with Engine=sqlserver-ee, include error in EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports without removing existing approved types; verify events and retention.
iac.label: Review RDS sqlserver error log export owner declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, Engine and EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports, then verify support and useful emission for error.
Have the database and logging owners approve event content, redaction, access, retention, KMS and ingestion cost while preserving existing exports.
Apply an owner-reviewed full export configuration including error and verify the corresponding CloudWatch log streams receive new events.
aws.cb.rds.sqlserver_error_log_export.summary: An RDS sqlserver-ee instance lacks one or more of error in EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports, leaving required database log exports undeclared.

caveats: Only Engine names beginning sqlserver are applicable. A parameter value alone does not prove connection behavior or client certificate verification; a shared group change can affect other instances.

cli.label: Inspect exact instance and attached groups

iac.code: For DBInstanceArn with Engine=sqlserver, declare ParameterGroupValues.rds.force_ssl=1 in a custom owner-managed DB parameter group, review all consumers and plan TLS validation.
iac.label: Review RDS sqlserver TLS parameter declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, Engine, every attached parameter group and its effective rds.force_ssl value for this sqlserver instance.
Have the database owner review shared parameter-group consumers, client TLS and certificate compatibility, backup readiness and reboot window.
Apply a reviewed parameter-group change to rds.force_ssl=1, reboot if required, then test encrypted connections and rejection of plaintext.
aws.cb.rds.sqlserver_force_ssl_parameter.summary: An RDS sqlserver instance has rds.force_ssl other than 1 in its attached DB parameter group, so the captured TLS enforcement setting is off.

caveats: AllowVersionUpgrade permits eligible upgrades; it is not evidence that the engine is already current. An upgrade can alter query behavior or client compatibility, so the owner must validate before maintenance.

cli.label: Apply the owner-approved Redshift cluster setting

iac.code: Set ClusterIdentifier owner declaration AllowVersionUpgrade true after engine compatibility and maintenance-window review.
iac.label: Review provisioned cluster declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift setting or migration guidance

steps: Inspect current engine version, maintenance window, workload compatibility and backup/recovery plan with the cluster owner.
Approve automatic version upgrades and schedule application testing for maintenance-window changes.
Enable AllowVersionUpgrade, then verify the property and monitor the subsequent maintenance event and client behavior.
aws.cb.redshift.allow_version_upgrade.summary: The provisioned Redshift cluster has AllowVersionUpgrade false, so automatic eligible version upgrades are disabled.

caveats: The check reads LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled only and does not prove log delivery or user-activity content. User activity events additionally require enable_user_activity_logging=true in the cluster parameter group.

cli.code: aws redshift enable-logging --cluster-identifier <CLUSTER_ID> --log-destination-type cloudwatch --log-exports connectionlog userlog useractivitylog --region <REGION>
cli.label: Enable owner-reviewed CloudWatch audit log exports

iac.code: Set LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled through an owner-managed Redshift audit logging configuration with approved CloudWatch destination, retention, access and user-activity parameter.
iac.label: Review cluster logging or TLS declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift audit or TLS guidance

steps: Inspect current logging destination, log group or S3 bucket access, retention and privacy requirements.
Have the audit and data owners approve CloudWatch exports for connection, user and user activity logs and confirm delivery permissions and cost.
Enable the reviewed exports, verify LoggingEnabled and inspect delivered events; separately enable the user-activity database parameter if that log is required.
aws.cb.redshift.audit_logging.summary: Redshift DescribeLoggingStatus reports LoggingEnabled false for this cluster, so external audit-log export is off.

caveats: The evaluator joins KMS metadata; a missing key row is unknown rather than evidence of AWS-managed encryption. The documented in-place modify flow explicitly covers enabling encryption on an unencrypted cluster; do not assume an existing encrypted cluster can switch keys with the same flag.

cli.label: Inspect cluster snapshots before key migration

iac.code: Set cluster encryption to a customer managed KMS key with explicit key policy and grants. For an encrypted cluster with the wrong key, plan an owner-reviewed restore or replacement rather than an unverified in-place key switch.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect the cluster Encrypted and KmsKeyId fields and join the exact key to KMS KeyManager, state, policy and grants.

Have the data and KMS owners approve a customer managed key, recovery point and tested migration path; plan replacement or snapshot restore if the current encrypted cluster cannot change key in place.
Migrate or restore using the reviewed key, verify the resulting cluster key joins to KeyManager=CUSTOMER, then test clients and recovery.
aws.cb.redshift.cmk_encryption.summary: Redshift is unencrypted or the joined KMS key has KeyManager other than CUSTOMER; this check requires a customer managed KMS key.

caveats: Redshift modifies the cluster by migrating data to a new encrypted cluster; the workload may be read-only or degraded depending on node type and size, and backup creation can pause until completion. Disable incompatible cross-Region snapshot copy first; HSM encryption requires a different migration.

cli.label: Apply the owner-approved Redshift cluster setting

iac.code: Set Encrypted true with an owner-approved KmsKeyId in the cluster declaration, with a migration, backup, KMS grants and workload-impact plan.
iac.label: Review provisioned cluster declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift setting or migration guidance

steps: Inspect cluster size, node type, cross-Region snapshot copy, KMS key permissions and a restorable prechange backup.
Have the data and KMS owners approve a key and maintenance window for Redshift’s automatic migration to an encrypted cluster.
Enable KMS encryption using the reviewed key, monitor migration and verify data, snapshots, clients and the Encrypted field afterward.
aws.cb.redshift.encrypted.summary: The Redshift cluster Encrypted field is false, so cluster storage and snapshots do not meet this encryption check.

caveats: The source short-circuits when Encrypted is false and does not inspect logging until encryption passes. Enabling KMS encryption triggers Redshift data migration with node-dependent workload impact; logging status alone does not prove delivery.

cli.label: Inspect cluster encryption and parameter-group settings
Start owner-approved KMS encryption migration if needed

cli.code: aws redshift enable-logging --cluster-identifier <CLUSTER_ID> --log-destination-type cloudwatch --log-exports connectionlog userlog useractivitylog --region <REGION>
cli.label: Enable owner-reviewed CloudWatch audit log exports

iac.code: Set Encrypted true with an approved KmsKeyId and LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled true in owner-managed cluster and audit declarations; stage backup, migration, CloudWatch retention and client checks.
iac.label: Review cluster logging or TLS declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift audit or TLS guidance

steps: Inspect both Encrypted and LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled, current snapshots, KMS permissions and audit delivery settings.
Have the data and audit owners plan KMS encryption migration where needed and a CloudWatch logging destination with privacy and cost controls.
Enable the missing setting in a controlled sequence, verify both exact fields and check data, client and log delivery after migration.
aws.cb.redshift.encrypted_and_logging.summary: The Redshift cluster is unencrypted, or it is encrypted but DescribeLoggingStatus reports audit logging disabled.

caveats: Redshift restarts when this setting changes. COPY or UNLOAD can fail if endpoint, DNS, NAT or policy paths are missing; Redshift Spectrum has separate routing behavior.

cli.label: Apply the owner-approved Redshift cluster setting

iac.code: Set EnhancedVpcRouting true in the owner-managed cluster declaration only after VPC endpoint, DNS, policy and restart validation.
iac.label: Review provisioned cluster declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift setting or migration guidance

steps: Inspect the cluster VPC, COPY/UNLOAD sources, endpoint policies, DNS, NAT and cross-Region data paths.
Have the network and data owners stage the required VPC endpoints or NAT routes and approve a restart window.
Enable EnhancedVpcRouting, verify the property after restart and test each COPY and UNLOAD workflow.
aws.cb.redshift.enhanced_vpc_routing.summary: The provisioned Redshift cluster has EnhancedVpcRouting false, so COPY and UNLOAD traffic is not forced through its VPC route controls.

caveats: The evaluator counts any matching snapshot, including manual or in-progress; it does not prove a recent, completed or restorable snapshot. Automated snapshots can be deleted when retention becomes zero.

cli.label: Inspect snapshots for the exact cluster
Create an owner-approved manual recovery point

iac.code: Declare an owner-approved automated snapshot retention and recovery schedule for ClusterIdentifier; separately document a named manual redshift_snapshot and periodic restore tests when needed.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect DescribeClusterSnapshots for the exact ClusterIdentifier, including snapshot status, type and age; confirm inventory is complete.
Have the data owner approve a recovery point, automated snapshot retention and storage cost; create a named manual snapshot if an immediate recovery point is needed.
Wait for the snapshot to finish, verify it belongs to the cluster and test a restore separately; rerun the inventory join without equating mere snapshot presence with recovery readiness.
aws.cb.redshift.has_snapshot.summary: No collected Redshift snapshot matches this ClusterIdentifier; a snapshot of any type is counted, regardless of age or restore readiness.

caveats: This conjunctive predicate does not fail every publicly accessible cluster or every world-open rule by itself. A route-table declaration and broad rule do not prove effective reachability; shared security groups and endpoint changes can break other clients.

cli.label: Disable public access after private-client migration

iac.code: Declare PubliclyAccessible=false and an owner-approved private client path; review subnet group routes and attached security group declarations, then stage a reversible cutover before reducing world ingress.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect PubliclyAccessible, endpoint, cluster subnet group and each subnet route to the Internet Gateway; inspect attached security group ingress with rule IDs.
Have network and database owners stage private access for all clients and approve disabling public accessibility and restricting the exact open security group rules.
Disable public access after client cutover, remove owner-reviewed world rules where safe, recollect subnet and route inventory and test intended private connectivity.
aws.cb.redshift.internet_exposed.summary: A publicly accessible Redshift endpoint joins to a cluster subnet with an Internet Gateway default route and a VPC security group allowing world CIDRs on all TCP ports.

caveats: An absent collected KmsKeyId on an already encrypted cluster can indicate inventory incompleteness; do not blindly re-encrypt it. Enabling KMS encryption migrates to a new encrypted cluster and can make workloads read-only during migration; disable incompatible cross-Region snapshot copy first.

cli.label: Inspect chosen KMS key and policy
Start approved encryption migration if unencrypted

iac.code: Declare Encrypted=true and an owner-approved KmsKeyId in the provisioned cluster configuration, with explicit migration, backup, KMS grants and workload-impact review.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect Encrypted, KmsKeyId, cluster node type, cross-Region snapshot copy and the key policy and grants.
Have the data and KMS owners approve a key, restorable backup, maintenance window and Redshift encryption migration.
Enable KMS encryption with the reviewed key only where the cluster is unencrypted; verify both collected fields and recovery after Redshift migration.
aws.cb.redshift.kms_key_declared.summary: The Redshift cluster is unencrypted or its KmsKeyId is absent; both Encrypted=true and a declared KMS key identifier are required.

caveats: The predicate checks configuration only; it does not prove a patch has been applied or a backup is usable. Version upgrades can change compatibility and need application testing.

cli.label: Raise retention where below seven days

iac.code: Declare AllowVersionUpgrade=true and AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod>=7 in the cluster owner configuration after patch-compatibility and recovery review.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect both fields and current engine version, maintenance window, pending changes and completed recovery points.
Have the database owner approve version compatibility testing and a maintenance window; approve a retention increase to at least seven days without reducing a longer policy.
Enable version upgrades and raise retention only where deficient, then verify both fields and test workload and recovery behavior independently.
aws.cb.redshift.maintenance_settings.summary: Redshift AllowVersionUpgrade is false or AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is below seven days; both configuration conditions must hold.

caveats: Multi-AZ eligibility and costs depend on node type, node count and subnet coverage. Conversion can require extra capacity and affects monitoring views, pause/resume behavior and client failover testing.

cli.label: Apply the owner-approved Redshift cluster setting

iac.code: Set MultiAZ Enabled in a supported owner-managed Redshift cluster after RG/RA3 eligibility, subnet and capacity checks.
iac.label: Review provisioned cluster declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift setting or migration guidance

steps: Inspect node type, subnet group AZ coverage, current capacity, endpoint clients and recovery objectives with the data owner.
Verify supported RG or RA3 deployment, eligible Region, at least three AZ-capable subnets and any required node or monitoring-query changes.
Enable MultiAZ in a planned change, then verify two-AZ status, connection continuity and recovery monitoring.
aws.cb.redshift.multi_az.summary: The Redshift cluster MultiAZ field is Disabled rather than Enabled.

caveats: ModifyCluster has no DBName field, so an in-place cluster setting command would be invalid. SQL-level database renames may not change the cluster metadata field this predicate reads.

iac.code: Set DBName to an owner-reviewed nondefault value in a new cluster declaration, then migrate data, client URLs and grants.
iac.label: Review replacement cluster declaration

steps: Inspect database references in BI tools, ETL jobs, JDBC URLs, grants and cluster restore procedures.
Have the data owner plan a replacement cluster with a reviewed initial DBName other than dev and migrate data and dependencies.
Create and validate the replacement from the complete reviewed declaration, update clients and verify the new DBName before cutover.
aws.cb.redshift.non_default_database_nam.summary: The Redshift cluster DBName remains the default dev value in DescribeClusters.

caveats: ModifyCluster has no MasterUsername field; an in-place flag would be invalid. Replacement and credential migration can interrupt authentication, so no deletion or automatic cutover command is offered.

iac.code: Set MasterUsername to a reviewed nondefault value in a new owner-managed cluster declaration and migrate credentials, grants and clients.
iac.label: Review replacement cluster declaration

steps: Inspect the current cluster, admin clients, secrets rotation, grants and all integration references to the master user.
Have the data owner plan a replacement cluster with a reviewed nondefault master name, preserving data, grants, network and encryption settings.
Create and validate the replacement from a complete reviewed declaration, migrate clients and credentials, then verify MasterUsername before cutover.
aws.cb.redshift.non_default_master_usern.summary: The Redshift cluster MasterUsername is the default awsuser value, rather than an owner-chosen administrator name.

caveats: The source reads the configuration flag, not route reachability or security-group exposure. Disabling public access immediately can interrupt clients that lack private connectivity.

cli.label: Apply the owner-approved Redshift cluster setting

iac.code: Set PubliclyAccessible false in the owner-managed cluster declaration after private client connectivity is validated.
iac.label: Review provisioned cluster declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift setting or migration guidance

steps: Inspect every BI, ETL and administrative client that connects through the public endpoint and its current security groups.
Provide approved private VPC, VPN or transit connectivity and test clients before removing public addressing.
Set PubliclyAccessible false, verify the property and endpoint path, and confirm authorized clients still connect privately.
aws.cb.redshift.not_publicly_accessible.summary: The provisioned Redshift cluster PubliclyAccessible field is true, so its endpoint is configured for public addressing.

caveats: A parameter group can be shared by multiple clusters; changing it may affect all of them. Static parameter changes can require reboot, and enabling TLS without client certificate preparation can interrupt connections.

cli.label: Inspect cluster encryption and parameter-group settings

iac.code: Set ParameterGroupValues.require_ssl true in the owner-managed cluster parameter group only after checking all attached clusters, certificate trust, maintenance reboot and client TLS readiness.
iac.label: Review cluster logging or TLS declaration

references.title: Official Amazon Redshift audit or TLS guidance

steps: Inspect the cluster parameter group, its require_ssl value, shared-cluster consumers and every JDBC or ODBC client TLS mode.
Have the database owner approve require_ssl=true and validate certificate trust and client compatibility in a maintenance window.
Apply the reviewed parameter change, reboot if required, verify ParameterGroupValues.require_ssl and reject a test plaintext connection.
aws.cb.redshift.require_ssl.summary: The Redshift cluster parameter group does not present require_ssl as true, so database clients are not forced to use TLS by this setting.

caveats: The evaluator accepts any protocol whose port range covers the endpoint port and protocol -1 without explicit ports; it does not require actual public route reachability. Shared security groups can serve other workloads, so removal needs dependency review.

cli.label: Remove only the owner-reviewed world ingress rule

iac.code: Replace world-CIDR ingress covering the Redshift endpoint port in the owning security group declaration with approved private CIDRs or group references after all attached clients are reviewed.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect the endpoint port and all attached security group rule IDs, IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs, protocols and port ranges.
Have the security group owner stage approved private CIDRs or referenced groups for database clients; identify only exact world-CIDR rules covering the evaluated port.
After client migration, revoke the approved rule ID and verify intended connections and the fresh security group inventory.
aws.cb.redshift.security_group_port_rest.summary: A Redshift attached security group has world-CIDR ingress whose protocol or port range includes the endpoint port, or port 5439 when that field is absent.

caveats: This check reads the retention number, not actual snapshot age or restore success. Setting retention to zero deletes automated snapshots; do not lower a longer existing policy to seven days.

iac.code: Set AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod to an owner-approved value of at least seven days in the cluster declaration, without shortening a longer recovery policy.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect the exact retention value, node type, snapshot schedule, current completed snapshots and backup costs.
Have the data owner approve raising AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod to at least seven days and a recovery window; preserve any longer existing setting.
Apply the reviewed increase, verify the field after modification and inspect later snapshot completion and restore viability separately.
aws.cb.redshift.snapshot_retention_7_day.summary: Redshift AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is below seven days, limiting the automated recovery window measured by this setting.

caveats: The condition checks only list membership, not CloudWatch delivery or retention. Replacing the export list without preserving an existing useractivitylog choice may reduce audit coverage and can incur logging cost.

cli.label: Apply a complete owner-reviewed export list

iac.code: In namespace logExports, include connectionlog and userlog and preserve other approved values. Manage destination retention and permissions in the logging owner stack, then verify real records after the namespace update.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect the namespace logExports and the destination log groups, retention, access and current useractivitylog choice.
Have the database and logging owners approve a full export list containing both connectionlog and userlog while preserving any other required exports.
Update the namespace with that reviewed list and verify new connection and user log records arrive.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.connection_use.summary: A Redshift Serverless namespace fails when logExports lacks connectionlog or userlog, leaving required connection or user activity records unexported.

caveats: Enabling VPC routing without necessary endpoints or egress can break data loads and exports. The flag alone does not prove that route tables or endpoint policies are correct.

iac.code: Set enhancedVpcRouting=true in the workgroup owner declaration, and provision reviewed subnet routes, endpoint policies and security groups. Verify data-transfer traffic and rollback readiness.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect enhancedVpcRouting, workgroup subnets, route tables, security groups and current data-transfer dependencies.
Have the network and database owners stage the required S3 and service endpoints or NAT paths, then approve VPC routing.
Enable enhanced VPC routing and validate COPY, UNLOAD and other data transfers through the intended network path.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.enhanced_vpc_r.summary: A Redshift Serverless workgroup fails when enhancedVpcRouting is not true, leaving data traffic outside its selected VPC routing path.

caveats: Changing the username can break clients and secret references; coordinate the credential rotation and connection cutover. The check compares only the literal admin and does not assess password strength or IAM access.

cli.label: Apply a reviewed non-default administrator username

iac.code: Set adminUsername to the approved non-default value in the namespace owner declaration and rotate or update managed credentials, connection strings and runbooks. Verify admin access and applications after deployment.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect adminUsername, managed-password mode, application connection strings and any automation that uses the administrator account.
Have the database and secret owners choose a non-default username and stage updated client credentials and rollback.
Update the namespace administrator username and verify authentication and dependent jobs before closing the finding.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.non_default_ad.summary: A Redshift Serverless namespace fails when adminUsername is exactly admin, leaving a predictable administrator login name.

caveats: dbName is a CreateNamespace field but absent from UpdateNamespace; no in-place rename flag is offered for this check. Replacement can interrupt clients and incur data migration cost; a separate SQL database rename would not necessarily change the namespace dbName field.

iac.code: Use a new namespace declaration with dbName different from dev and migrate datasets, grants, secrets, workgroup association and client endpoints through a reviewed cutover. Verify the new namespace dbName and retain rollback.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect dbName, database consumers, datasets, grants and namespace snapshot or migration options.
Have the database owner design a replacement namespace with a non-default initial database name; UpdateNamespace does not expose dbName.
Create the reviewed replacement, migrate data and grants, test workgroups and clients, then cut over and verify the new dbName.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.non_default_da.summary: A Redshift Serverless namespace fails when its initial dbName is exactly dev, leaving the default database name in the namespace detail.

caveats: The flag does not establish actual route reachability or effective authentication. Closing public access can interrupt external clients; stage VPN, private network or approved endpoint migration first.

cli.label: Disable public workgroup accessibility after private cutover

iac.code: Set publiclyAccessible=false in the workgroup owner declaration, migrate clients to approved private connectivity, review security groups and verify both access and internet denial.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect publiclyAccessible, workgroup networking, authorized client locations and DNS or connection strings.
Have the network and database owners establish private connectivity and validate every client path before closing public access.
Set publiclyAccessible=false and verify the workgroup endpoint is private and approved clients can still connect.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.not_publicly_a.summary: A Redshift Serverless workgroup fails when publiclyAccessible is true, exposing an internet-reachable endpoint setting.

caveats: The evaluator requires an exact parameterKey=require_ssl and parameterValue=true pair. Replacing configParameters without preserving other values can change workload behavior; client compatibility needs review.

cli.label: Apply the complete reviewed workgroup parameter list

iac.code: In workgroup configParameters, set parameterKey=require_ssl with parameterValue=true and preserve other approved parameters. Verify clients use TLS and that plaintext attempts fail after deployment.
iac.label: Review the Redshift Serverless owner declaration

steps: Inspect the full workgroup configParameters list and test current client TLS support.
Have the database owner approve require_ssl=true while preserving every other parameter and plan client certificate changes.
Update the complete reviewed parameter list, verify the workgroup setting and test TLS-required and rejected plaintext connections.
aws.cb.redshiftserverless.require_ssl.summary: A Redshift Serverless workgroup fails when configParameters lacks require_ssl=true, allowing connections without the required SSL setting.

caveats: The condition checks existence only; it does not prove indexing coverage, a designated aggregator, search permissions or search freshness. Indexing can expose resource metadata to authorized search users.

iac.code: Declare a Resource Explorer index in the approved account and Region, and review the resourceexplorer2_index inventory, search permissions and intended aggregation strategy. Verify indexing progress before asserting usable search.
iac.label: Review the owner declaration

steps: Inspect account indexes from the intended Region and confirm that the index inventory is complete and current.
Ask the Resource Explorer owner to choose an approved Region, resource indexing scope and access policy before creating an index.
Create a local index in the approved Region, wait for indexing, then verify ListIndexes and search access for authorized users.
aws.cb.resourceexplorer2.index_exists.summary: The account scope fails when the complete Resource Explorer index inventory is empty; resources cannot be found through an account index.

caveats: A CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE source fails this exact predicate. A CA absent from complete same-account inventory is MANUAL because it may be cross-account; do not replace it based only on missing local evidence.

A CA KeyAlgorithm is chosen at creation, not converted in place. Switching a live trust anchor can invalidate existing client certificates or credential sessions; no automatic CA creation or old-anchor deletion is offered.

cli.label: Inspect the linked or proposed Private CA
Apply only a reviewed source after certificate migration

iac.code: For trustAnchorArn, select source.sourceType=AWS_ACM_PCA and source.sourceData.acmPcaArn only after the referenced acmpca_certificate_authority has Status=ACTIVE and CertificateAuthorityConfiguration.KeyAlgorithm in ML_DSA_44/65/87; stage certificate issuance, overlap and client validation.
iac.label: Review PKI and trust-anchor owner declarations

steps: Inspect the exact trustAnchorArn and sourceType; when AWS_ACM_PCA, resolve sourceData.acmPcaArn and inspect the CA Status and KeyAlgorithm.
Have the PKI and workload owners create or select a compatible active ML-DSA Private CA, issue and test replacement certificates, and plan trust and client overlap.
After certificate and identity migration are ready, update the owner-reviewed trust anchor source or replace the anchor, then verify new credential sessions and old-client retirement.
aws.cb.rolesanywhere.trust_anchor_pqc.summary: A Roles Anywhere trust anchor is not backed by an ACTIVE AWS Private CA with an ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65 or ML_DSA_87 KeyAlgorithm under this certificate-trust control.

caveats: Automatic renewal depends on billing, registrar eligibility and current contact details; a true flag does not guarantee successful renewal. The operation can lead to future renewal charges.

iac.code: Set Detail.AutoRenew=true in the registrar owner record through the supported Route 53 Domains API, and reconcile the actual domain detail. Keep expiry and billing alerts independent of the toggle.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect AutoRenew, ExpirationDate, registrar contact status and billing ownership for the exact domain.
Have the domain owner confirm renewal intent, payment method and TLD rules, then enable automatic renewal.
Verify AutoRenew=true and retain separate expiry alerts and contact monitoring.
aws.cb.route53.domain_auto_renew.summary: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AutoRenew is not true, increasing the chance of registration lapse at expiry.

caveats: The threshold uses calendar days at capture time and can cross a day boundary before the API change. Renewal is billable, TLD-specific and asynchronous; AutoRenew alone may not satisfy the immediate lead-time condition.

iac.code: Monitor Detail.ExpirationDate against capture_time with a 30-calendar-day alert, and record registrar billing, AutoRenew and owner approval. Update the domain owner record only after a paid renewal completes and the new expiry is verified.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect ExpirationDate, AutoRenew, TLD renewal lead time, billing and registrar contact state.
Have the domain owner approve a renewal duration and charge, using the current expiry year from GetDomainDetail.
Renew before the TLD cutoff, track the operation and verify the new ExpirationDate exceeds the 30-day threshold.
aws.cb.route53.domain_expires_after_30_d.summary: A Route 53 domain fails when its ExpirationDate is fewer than 30 calendar days after snapshot capture, leaving too little renewal lead time.

caveats: Some registries delete domains before their displayed expiry if renewal is late. Renewal is billable and asynchronous; a submitted operation does not extend the date until completed.

iac.code: Escalate Detail.ExpirationDate within seven calendar days of capture_time to the registrar owner with billing approval and TLD cutoff details. Confirm the paid renewal and updated expiry in GetDomainDetail.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect ExpirationDate and registrar operation status immediately, including billing and TLD-specific grace rules.
Have the domain owner approve a renewal duration and charge using the current expiry year, then submit before the registry cutoff.
Track completion and verify the new ExpirationDate is at least seven calendar days away.
aws.cb.route53.domain_expires_after_7_da.summary: A Route 53 domain fails when its ExpirationDate is fewer than seven calendar days after snapshot capture, requiring urgent renewal review.

caveats: No universal safe renewal command is offered for an expired domain: registry redemption and restore rules vary by TLD, and the name may no longer be recoverable. The one-minute tolerance is only a capture-time comparison.

iac.code: Treat Detail.ExpirationDate before capture_time minus one minute as a registrar incident. Follow the TLD-specific restoration runbook and verify ownership, DNS continuity and the new expiration date; no IaC flag can restore a lost registration.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect the live domain detail and registrar status to confirm whether the registration has expired or the snapshot is stale.
Escalate to the domain and registrar owners for the TLD-specific renewal or restoration path, associated charges and DNS continuity plan.
Verify restored registration, authoritative DNS and a future ExpirationDate before closing the finding.
aws.cb.route53.domain_not_expired.summary: A Route 53 domain fails when its ExpirationDate is earlier than snapshot capture by more than one minute, indicating expired registration in the captured detail.

caveats: The check evaluates AdminPrivacy only and does not prove privacy for other contact types. Some TLDs require matching privacy values or do not support the operation; do not disable privacy to make values match.

iac.code: Set Detail.AdminPrivacy=true in the registrar owner record and review RegistrantPrivacy, TechPrivacy and BillingPrivacy for TLD requirements. Track the registrar operation and verify the final detail.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect AdminPrivacy and the privacy state of registrant, technical and billing contacts for the domain.
Have the registrar owner confirm TLD support and approve privacy for all required contact types.
Enable admin contact privacy, track the returned operation to completion and verify the contact privacy fields.
aws.cb.route53.domain_privacy_protection.summary: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AdminPrivacy is not true, leaving the administrative contact without the requested WHOIS privacy setting.

caveats: The lock can delay an intentional transfer; coordinate any planned transfer window and registrar/TLD restrictions. A status entry is not proof of all account access protections.

iac.code: Require clientTransferProhibited in Detail.StatusList for domains under Route 53 registrar ownership and document any time-bounded approved transfer exception. Verify the registrar status after the API operation.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect StatusList, domain ownership, any pending transfer and the registrar operation state.
Have the domain owner confirm that a transfer is not planned and enable the transfer lock.
Track the registrar operation and verify clientTransferProhibited appears in StatusList.
aws.cb.route53.domain_transfer_lock.summary: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.StatusList lacks clientTransferProhibited, leaving registrar transfer lock absent.

caveats: Private hosted zones are not applicable. A configuration ARN alone does not prove log delivery; Route 53 needs log-group write permission, and DNS queries may contain sensitive names and incur log costs.

cli.label: Inspect query logging for the exact hosted zone
Create the owner-approved public-zone query log configuration

iac.code: For Config.PrivateZone=false, declare QueryLoggingConfigs.QueryLoggingConfigs.CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn to a same-account us-east-1 log group, with a reviewed Route 53 write resource policy and retention. Verify delivered DNS query records after creation.
iac.label: Review the DNS and logging owner declarations

references.title: AWS Route 53 public DNS query logging guide

steps: Confirm the hosted zone is public and inspect its current query logging configurations and DNS query volume.
Have the DNS and logging owners create or select a same-account CloudWatch Logs group in us-east-1, with reviewed resource policy, retention and access.
Create the query logging configuration for the reviewed zone and log group, then verify real DNS query events arrive.
aws.cb.route53.public_zone_query_logging.summary: A public Route 53 hosted zone fails when no query logging configuration has a CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn; private zones are outside this condition.

caveats: The regional check accepts any historical Clarify-image job; it does not prove that the current models were assessed, that the job completed, or that bias findings were addressed. Regions without models are not applicable.

iac.code: Declare a model-linked ProcessingJobName and AppSpecification.ImageUri containing the approved sagemaker-clarify-processing image, with reviewed datasets, role, encryption, outputs and result review.
iac.label: Review SageMaker clarify job exists declaration

steps: Inspect existing ProcessingJobName and AppSpecification.ImageUri values, then identify the relevant model, representative dataset and approved bias or explainability question.
Have the data and ML owners review input data consent, protected attribute handling, Clarify configuration, processing role, encrypted outputs and budget.
Run a reviewed Clarify processing job and inspect its completed output and image URI; retain the assessment for the model owner.
aws.cb.sagemaker.clarify_job_exists.summary: A Region with SageMaker models has no processing job whose AppSpecification.ImageUri names the SageMaker Clarify processing image.

caveats: UpdateDomain does not accept AuthMode, so an IAM-authenticated domain cannot be switched in place. AWS states certain VPC/interface-endpoint/IP-only access restrictions require IAM AuthMode; SSO may be incompatible with that architecture. A linked identifier alone does not prove users have assignments.

iac.code: Declare DomainArn replacement with AuthMode=SSO, same-Region IAM Identity Center application, linked SingleSignOnApplicationArn or managed application ID, user assignments and safe migration of spaces and EFS data.
iac.label: Review SageMaker domain identity and migration declaration

steps: Inspect DomainArn, AuthMode and both SingleSignOn application fields, existing users, spaces, EFS data and application network restrictions.

Have identity and domain owners approve a new SSO domain in the same Region as IAM Identity Center and plan user, space, storage and access migration; decide whether IAM-only VPC or IP restrictions are a required exception.
Create the reviewed replacement domain with AuthMode=SSO, migrate and test users and data, then verify a linked application field and successful sign-in.
aws.cb.sagemaker.domain_sso.summary: SageMaker domain AuthMode is not SSO or it has no linked IAM Identity Center managed application identifier or ARN.

caveats: Endpoint configurations are immutable; existing live endpoints require a new config and deployment. A missing explicit KmsKeyId does not prove plaintext storage, and this field does not encrypt Nitro instance local storage.

cli.label: Deploy replacement configuration to an approved endpoint

iac.code: Declare a new EndpointConfigArn with reviewed KmsKeyId, key grants and all production variants; update dependent endpoints through staged deployment and retain rollback.
iac.label: Review hosting endpoint owner declaration

references.title: Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint config API
Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint deployment API

steps: Inspect the endpoint configuration, KmsKeyId, model variants, backing instance types and live endpoint consumers.
Have the hosting and KMS owners approve a key with grants, a new endpoint configuration and traffic-shift rollback.
Create the reviewed configuration, update each approved endpoint to it, monitor the new fleet and verify KmsKeyId and inference health.
aws.cb.sagemaker.endpoint_config_kms.summary: SageMaker endpoint configuration KmsKeyId is empty or absent, so the hosting ML storage volume lacks an explicit KMS key setting.

caveats: The check examines initial configuration counts, not live CurrentInstanceCount or real AZ redundancy. A serverless variant with no InitialInstanceCount is ignored by this source; forcing instances onto it would be invalid.

cli.label: Deploy replacement configuration to an approved endpoint

iac.code: Set ProductionVariants[].InitialInstanceCount>1 for affected provisioned variants in a new EndpointConfigArn, preserve serverless variants and test endpoint deployment and cost.
iac.label: Review hosting endpoint owner declaration

references.title: Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint config API
Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint deployment API

steps: Inspect every ProductionVariants entry, InitialInstanceCount, serverless status, endpoint traffic and autoscaling target.
Have hosting owners size at least two initial instances for affected provisioned variants, including capacity, cost and multi-AZ placement review.
Create a reviewed replacement endpoint configuration with higher counts and deploy it using controlled traffic shifting; verify variant health and current serving capacity.
aws.cb.sagemaker.endpoint_variants_more_.summary: At least one SageMaker production variant has InitialInstanceCount at or below one; this control requires more than one configured initial instance.

caveats: This source flags exactly one, unlike the sibling control that flags values at or below one; missing counts and serverless variants are not evidence of multi-instance resilience. Endpoint configuration replacement is required.

cli.label: Deploy replacement configuration to an approved endpoint

iac.code: Avoid ProductionVariants[].InitialInstanceCount=1 for reviewed provisioned variants in a new EndpointConfigArn, preserving model weights, serverless settings and staged endpoint traffic.
iac.label: Review hosting endpoint owner declaration

references.title: Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint config API
Official Amazon SageMaker endpoint deployment API

steps: Inspect each variant’s InitialInstanceCount, serving model, serverless mode and current endpoint capacity.
Have the hosting owner approve a replacement count above one where high availability is required, or document a reviewed exception for intentionally single-instance use.
Create and deploy a reviewed configuration with the chosen count, then verify its InitialInstanceCount and actual live capacity separately.
aws.cb.sagemaker.endpoint_variants_not_e.summary: At least one SageMaker production variant has InitialInstanceCount exactly one; this control flags that precise value.

caveats: Network isolation can break models that download artifacts or call external services at runtime. It is set at CreateModel and does not retrofit an existing model; the check does not prove broader VPC isolation.

iac.code: Set ModelArn replacement EnableNetworkIsolation=true after validating container code, artifact access and deployment cutover in the owner model declaration.
iac.label: Review model and endpoint owner declarations

steps: Inspect model container image, artifact loading, startup scripts, external API calls and current EnableNetworkIsolation.
Have the model owner remove or redesign network-dependent initialization and inference code, then approve an isolated replacement model.
Create the replacement with EnableNetworkIsolation=true, deploy it through a new endpoint configuration and test inference and artifact loading.
aws.cb.sagemaker.model_network_isolation.summary: SageMaker model EnableNetworkIsolation is false or absent, so the model container is not isolated from inbound and outbound network calls by this setting.

caveats: The regional check accepts one group with one approved version; it does not prove every model is registered or deployed from that version. Approval is a governance decision, not a command to rubber-stamp an untested package. Regions without models are not applicable.

iac.code: Declare ModelPackageGroupName and release workflow that yields ApprovedPackages>0 only for validated, owner-approved model package versions, with deployment lineage and rollback.
iac.label: Review SageMaker model registry approved package declaration

references.title: Official SageMaker update model package API

steps: Inspect model package groups and their approved package versions in the Region, and identify the deployment pipeline and approval authority.
Have the ML owner define a package group, register a vetted model version with lineage and tests, then separately approve the exact package ARN after review.
Verify the approved version appears in the group inventory and ensure future deployment workflows consume the governed package rather than an unrelated model.
aws.cb.sagemaker.model_registry_approved.summary: A Region with SageMaker models has no model package group whose ApprovedPackages count is positive.

caveats: CreateModel properties cannot be edited on the existing model; a replacement name and endpoint cutover are required. A present but empty VpcConfig satisfies this exact check, so separately validate Subnets and SecurityGroupIds.

iac.code: Declare ModelArn replacement with VpcConfig.Subnets and VpcConfig.SecurityGroupIds plus private artifact access, endpoint config, staged deployment and rollback.
iac.label: Review model and endpoint owner declarations

steps: Inspect the model definition, container artifact access, endpoint consumers and existing network routes.
Have the model and network owners approve a private VPC subnet and security group design with required S3, ECR and KMS paths.
Create a replacement model with VpcConfig, create and deploy an endpoint configuration referencing it, then test inference and verify the new VpcConfig.
aws.cb.sagemaker.model_vpc_config.summary: SageMaker model VpcConfig is absent, so the hosted model has no declared customer VPC attachment.

caveats: This check counts subnet IDs only and does not prove their route privacy or security-group policy. Existing model VpcConfig cannot be changed in place; a replacement model and dependent endpoint cutover are needed.

iac.code: Declare ModelArn replacement with nonempty VpcConfig.Subnets and reviewed SecurityGroupIds, including AZ, route, endpoint and rollback checks.
iac.label: Review model and endpoint owner declarations

steps: Inspect the exact VpcConfig.Subnets list, referenced security groups and serving endpoint dependencies.
Have network owners select accessible private subnets across the required AZs and verify artifact and service endpoints.
Create a replacement model with approved nonempty Subnets, redeploy dependent endpoint configuration and verify container connectivity.
aws.cb.sagemaker.model_vpc_subnets.summary: SageMaker model VpcConfig is absent or its Subnets list is empty, leaving no declared customer VPC subnet for the container.

caveats: The regional check accepts any single Scheduled schedule when any model exists; it does not prove coverage of every model or successful job executions. Regions without models are not applicable. A schedule incurs recurring processing and storage charges.

iac.code: Declare MonitoringScheduleName and MonitoringScheduleStatus=Scheduled per approved endpoint with data capture, baseline, job role, output and alerts; document model-to-schedule coverage separately.
iac.label: Review SageMaker monitoring schedule active declaration

steps: Inspect the models, deployed endpoints, captured inference data and every schedule status in the affected Region.
Have the ML and privacy owners define a model-specific baseline, data capture, schedule, execution role, destination and alert response; verify data consent and storage controls.
Create the reviewed schedule for a deployed endpoint, inspect its status and first processing-job outcome, and repeat for each model that needs monitoring.
aws.cb.sagemaker.monitoring_schedule_act.summary: A Region with SageMaker models has no monitoring schedule whose MonitoringScheduleStatus is Scheduled.

caveats: An unresolved KMS key join is UNKNOWN; do not infer manager from an alias or ARN shape. Existing notebook KmsKeyId cannot be switched through UpdateNotebookInstance, and deleting the old key can strand data.

iac.code: Use a customer managed KmsKeyId for the NotebookInstanceArn replacement and declare key policy, grants, backup, data migration and old-key retention explicitly.
iac.label: Review the SageMaker notebook owner declaration

steps: Inspect notebook KmsKeyId and join the exact KMS key to KeyManager, key state, policy and execution-role grants.
Have the notebook and KMS owners select a customer managed key and plan a replacement notebook plus artifact migration.
Create the reviewed replacement, restore content and verify its KmsKeyId resolves to KeyManager=CUSTOMER.
aws.cb.sagemaker.notebook_cmk.summary: SageMaker notebook has no KmsKeyId or its joined KMS key KeyManager is not CUSTOMER, so storage does not use a customer managed key.

caveats: UpdateNotebookInstance cannot attach or change SubnetId. An approved subnet does not prove route privacy, and replacement can change addresses, lifecycle behavior and user access.

iac.code: Declare an approved SubnetId and SecurityGroupIds for the NotebookInstanceArn replacement with private service routes, notebook migration and tested owner access.
iac.label: Review the SageMaker notebook owner declaration

steps: Inspect SubnetId, current access path, notebook artifacts, required endpoints and security groups.
Have the network owner choose a private subnet and security group with working DNS, KMS, S3 and service access.
Create a replacement notebook with the reviewed SubnetId and groups, migrate content and users, then verify the new subnet and client access.
aws.cb.sagemaker.notebook_in_vpc.summary: SageMaker notebook SubnetId is absent, so the notebook is not attached to a customer VPC subnet.

caveats: UpdateNotebookInstance cannot change KmsKeyId. The setting does not retroactively re-encrypt the old notebook’s data; migration and cleanup are separate owner-controlled tasks.

iac.code: Declare NotebookInstanceArn replacement with a reviewed KmsKeyId, key policy, backup and copied notebook data; preserve access to old encrypted content during migration.
iac.label: Review the SageMaker notebook owner declaration

steps: Inspect KmsKeyId, attached volume content, snapshot or backup path, execution role and KMS key grants.
Have notebook, storage and KMS owners approve a new key and a replacement notebook with a tested data-migration plan.
Create the replacement with reviewed KmsKeyId, restore notebook content, validate decryption and verify the new KmsKeyId.
aws.cb.sagemaker.notebook_kms_key.summary: SageMaker notebook KmsKeyId is absent, so this notebook’s storage volume has no declared customer-specified KMS key.

caveats: UpdateNotebookInstance does not accept DirectInternetAccess, so this is a replacement workflow. Disabling direct access without VPC endpoints or approved egress can break package installation, APIs and data connections.

iac.code: Declare NotebookInstanceArn owner replacement with DirectInternetAccess=Disabled, approved SubnetId, security groups, endpoint routes and notebook artifact migration.
iac.label: Review the SageMaker notebook owner declaration

steps: Inspect DirectInternetAccess, VPC subnet, security groups, notebook content, package repositories and required outbound services.
Have the notebook and network owners design a replacement with DirectInternetAccess=Disabled, private VPC connectivity and approved endpoints or egress.
Create the reviewed replacement, migrate notebooks and users, validate required private service access and verify the new setting is Disabled.
aws.cb.sagemaker.notebook_no_direct_inte.summary: SageMaker notebook DirectInternetAccess is Enabled, allowing the notebook’s direct internet path under this setting.

caveats: Lifecycle configuration scripts continue to run as root even when RootAccess=Disabled; review their source and execution-role permissions separately. The notebook may need to be stopped before updating and restarted afterward.

cli.label: Disable owner-approved notebook user root access

iac.code: Set NotebookInstanceArn RootAccess=Disabled in the notebook owner configuration, and review lifecycle scripts and execution-role privileges separately.
iac.label: Review the SageMaker notebook owner declaration

steps: Inspect RootAccess, existing privileged notebook workflows, lifecycle scripts and the owner’s recovery access path.
Have the notebook owner remove root-dependent user workflows and approve the configuration change during a stopped-instance maintenance window.
Set RootAccess=Disabled, start the notebook as required, verify ordinary user functions and inspect the new field.
aws.cb.sagemaker.notebook_root_access_di.summary: SageMaker notebook RootAccess is Enabled, allowing notebook users root access under this configuration.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. This field matters for peer traffic in distributed training; a single-instance job may have no inter-container path, but the source still flags false. Encryption can lengthen training.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Set EnableInterContainerTrafficEncryption=true on future TrainingJobArn jobs after distributed workload performance review.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect whether the run used multiple ML compute instances and review inter-container communication patterns and current flag.
Have the ML owner approve TLS overhead and compatibility testing for the next distributed training run.
Create a new job with EnableInterContainerTrafficEncryption=true, validate performance and verify the new job field; keep the old job finding historical.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_intercontainer.summary: SageMaker training job EnableInterContainerTrafficEncryption is false or absent, so distributed peer traffic is not covered by this job setting.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. Network isolation blocks all container network calls, including S3, though SageMaker can still handle S3 transfers separately; some managed images are incompatible.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Set EnableNetworkIsolation=true in future TrainingJobArn pipeline definitions only after container and data-access validation.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect the training image, algorithm, external API calls and data download behavior before isolating the next run.
Have the ML owner remove network-dependent container behavior or provide SageMaker-managed input/output paths and test compatibility.
Create a new job with EnableNetworkIsolation=true, validate training and artifact upload and verify the new field.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_network_isolat.summary: SageMaker training job EnableNetworkIsolation is false or absent, so its containers were allowed network calls under this setting.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. Missing KmsKeyId does not mean output is plaintext: SageMaker and S3 have default encryption. SageMaker cannot use SSE-KMS for output in S3 directory buckets; move the output path before requiring this field.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Declare OutputDataConfig.S3OutputPath in a compatible bucket and a reviewed KmsKeyId for future TrainingJobArn output, with key grants and old-object migration.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect the S3OutputPath, bucket type and current output encryption, and verify the execution role can use a proposed KMS key.
Have data and KMS owners approve a general-purpose S3 output bucket, key policy, retention and encryption migration for existing artifacts.
Create a new training job with a reviewed OutputDataConfig.KmsKeyId and verify new output object encryption; handle old artifacts separately.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_output_kms.summary: SageMaker training OutputDataConfig.KmsKeyId is empty or absent, so no explicit KMS key is declared for the job’s S3 output.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. The check tests an explicit key ID rather than proving all storage is otherwise unencrypted. Existing ephemeral training volumes cannot be retroactively re-keyed.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Set ResourceConfig.VolumeKmsKeyId on future TrainingJobArn declarations with KMS grants for the execution role and tested data recovery.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect ResourceConfig.InstanceType, volume size, storage use and current key grants for this historical job.
Have the ML and KMS owners approve a usable volume key and restart plan for future training runs.
Create a new job with ResourceConfig.VolumeKmsKeyId, verify its setting and workload success, and preserve the old run’s historical result.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_volume_kms.summary: SageMaker training ResourceConfig.VolumeKmsKeyId is empty or absent, so the ML storage volume lacks an explicit KMS key setting.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. A present but empty VpcConfig passes this exact check, so validate Subnets and SecurityGroupIds separately.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Declare TrainingJobArn for a new run with VpcConfig.Subnets and SecurityGroupIds plus private endpoints and artifact access; do not represent an old run as fixed.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect the completed job VpcConfig, input and output locations, execution role and network dependencies.
Have pipeline and network owners design private subnet and security-group access for the next run, including S3, KMS and service endpoints.
Create a new reviewed training job with VpcConfig and validate container access and collected configuration; retain the historical finding for the old run.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_vpc_config.summary: SageMaker training job VpcConfig is absent, so this run has no declared customer VPC attachment.

caveats: All completed training jobs are immutable history; a new job does not change the original finding. Subnet presence alone does not prove a private route or proper network access, and VPC subnets need sufficient free IP addresses.

cli.label: Create a new owner-reviewed training job

iac.code: Declare nonempty VpcConfig.Subnets and reviewed SecurityGroupIds on future TrainingJobArn jobs, with IP capacity and service endpoint checks.
iac.label: Review future training pipeline declaration

steps: Inspect exact Subnets, SecurityGroupIds, subnet IP capacity and input/output data paths.
Have network and ML owners approve nonempty private subnet IDs in a supported default-tenancy VPC and compatible security groups.
Start a new run with reviewed VpcConfig.Subnets, validate data and endpoint connectivity and preserve the older job result as historical.
aws.cb.sagemaker.training_vpc_subnets.summary: SageMaker training job VpcConfig is missing or its Subnets list is empty, leaving no declared customer VPC subnet for the run.

caveats: This calendar-day comparison differs from the separate elapsed-duration access check near day 90. An arbitrary read would only change the signal and would not prove a real application dependency; deletion is not offered from this evidence alone.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Apply the LastAccessedDate calendar policy to the owning application inventory, then fix legitimate consumer access or use a separately approved retention-aware decommission plan.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect the exact LastAccessedDate and evaluate the 90-calendar-day boundary using the snapshot capture date.
Ask the application and secret owners whether infrequent, emergency or suspended consumers still require this secret.
Restore a legitimate integration when broken, or plan owner-approved retirement with retention and rollback after all consumers are checked.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.accessed_within_90.summary: A secret has no LastAccessedDate or the calendar-day difference from capture exceeds 90, marking it stale under the calendar-day access control.

caveats: The source compares a full elapsed 90-day duration; it cannot prove the secret is safe to delete. Artificial retrieval is not a valid remediation and no automatic deletion command is provided.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Document LastAccessedDate and expected consumers in the owner secret declaration; use actual access and a reviewed lifecycle decision rather than timestamp manipulation.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect LastAccessedDate and the expected application access pattern before labeling the secret unused.
Have the owner check all real consumers, emergency-only use cases, retention and rollback obligations.
Repair a missing legitimate consumer integration or stage a separately approved retirement after dependency review; observe authentic access if use resumes.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.accessed_within_90.summary: A secret has no LastAccessedDate or its last access is more than 90 elapsed days old, indicating a possibly unused credential under this control.

caveats: A metadata edit without rotating the real credential is not an approved fix. The finding does not bind the backing credential or application consumers, so no universal safe mutation command is available.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Update the owner secret declaration and application credential workflow for LastChangedDate policy; require real credential rollover and verify clients, not a metadata-only touch.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect LastChangedDate, creation time and the credential system that the secret represents.
Have the application and credential owners verify that a real value change is required, design synchronized credential rollover and test rollback.
Change the underlying credential and secret value through the owner workflow, then verify clients and a new LastChangedDate.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.changed_within_365.summary: A secret has no LastChangedDate or its last value change was more than 365 calendar days before the snapshot, so this annual change control fails.

caveats: This source uses calendar-day age rather than an elapsed 90-times-24-hour threshold. Updating secret metadata alone is not a credential change; no generic secret-value command is safe without knowing the backing system.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Set the LastChangedDate/90-calendar-day operational control in the secret owner workflow and rotate the backing credential with application cutover, rather than touching metadata.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect the exact LastChangedDate and compare the 90-day calendar policy with the credential owner schedule.
Review rotation capability, downtime, consumer cache behavior and rollback for the backing credential.
Perform an owner-approved real credential rollover, update the secret value, and verify every client before checking the new change date.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.changed_within_90_.summary: A secret has no LastChangedDate or its last value change was more than 90 calendar days before capture, failing the shorter change interval.

caveats: Changing KmsKeyId can affect access to current and earlier versions. Keep the previous key enabled and decryption grants available until all required versions and rollback paths are validated. A key identifier that is not the AWS alias alone is not proof of customer ownership.

iac.code: Set KmsKeyId in the secret owner declaration only after confirming kms_key.Metadata.KeyMetadata.KeyManager=CUSTOMER and key policies for all current and historical readers.
iac.label: Update the owning secret declaration

steps: Inspect the exact secret ARN and KmsKeyId, resolve the KMS key manager, and identify all readers and older secret versions.
Have the KMS and application owners approve a customer-managed key with correct encrypt/decrypt policy, grant and rotation arrangements.
Change the secret key and verify current and historical version decryption as well as every application reader before retiring old-key permissions.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.cmk_encryption.summary: A secret has no KmsKeyId, uses alias/aws/secretsmanager, or resolves to a non-CUSTOMER KMS key, so it fails the customer-managed encryption condition.

caveats: This source accepts some restrictive account, organization or private-network conditions; an absent resource policy is NOT_APPLICABLE, not evidence of a public grant.

A full resource-policy replacement can revoke applications or cross-account consumers. The policy file must be prepared and approved separately; no secret value or policy blob is interpolated into the command.

cli.label: Inspect the complete current resource policy
Apply an owner-reviewed complete policy document

iac.code: In the secret owner declaration, inspect Policy.ResourcePolicy.Statement.Effect, Principal and Condition; narrow only the actual public Allow and retain approved readers with a separately reviewed complete policy document.
iac.label: Review the complete secret resource policy declaration

steps: Inspect the full resource policy for the exact secret ARN and identify the granting Allow statements, principals, actions and conditions.
Have the secret owner and every legitimate reader review a replacement policy document that narrows the actual granting statement while preserving required access.
Apply the reviewed complete policy with the public-policy block and verify authorized readers and the public-policy analyzer result.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.policy_not_public.summary: A secret resource policy has an Allow principal that the account-aware public-policy check treats as public, exposing secret access through a broad grant.

caveats: This source recognizes only its listed owner, account, organization, principal or source condition keys; a condition accepted by another policy check may not satisfy this one. An absent resource policy is NOT_APPLICABLE.

A full resource-policy replacement can revoke applications or cross-account consumers. The policy file must be prepared and approved separately; no secret value or policy blob is interpolated into the command.

cli.label: Inspect the complete current resource policy
Apply an owner-reviewed complete policy document

iac.code: In the secret owner declaration, inspect Policy.ResourcePolicy.Statement.Effect, Principal and Condition; narrow only the actual public Allow and retain approved readers with a separately reviewed complete policy document.
iac.label: Review the complete secret resource policy declaration

steps: Inspect the full resource policy for the exact secret ARN and identify the granting Allow statements, principals, actions and conditions.
Have the secret owner and every legitimate reader review a replacement policy document that narrows the actual granting statement while preserving required access.
Apply the reviewed complete policy with the public-policy block and verify authorized readers and the public-policy analyzer result.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.policy_prohibit_pu.summary: A secret resource policy has a wildcard-principal Allow without a recognized restricting condition, so its resource policy permits perimeter exposure.

caveats: Replicas in another PrimaryRegion are NOT_APPLICABLE. A schedule expression without AutomaticallyAfterDays is UNKNOWN under this evaluator, and a manual timestamp change does not establish a completed rotation.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Keep PrimaryRegion and RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays aligned with the owner rotation workflow; monitor LastRotatedDate and actual application authentication after each rotation.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Check PrimaryRegion, RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays, LastRotatedDate and rotation status for the exact secret ARN.
Have the credential owner repair the rotation mechanism, Lambda permissions and target credential access; test rollback and application refresh.
Run a reviewed rotation only after preconditions are satisfied and verify a completed rotation within the configured interval.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.rotated_as_schedul.summary: A primary-region secret has no RotationRules or its LastRotatedDate/CreatedDate age exceeds RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays, indicating missed scheduled rotation.

caveats: Never-rotated secrets fail. This source uses elapsed-day age, and a RotateSecret request alone is not proof that the asynchronous rotation completed.

cli.label: Inspect the exact secret metadata without retrieving its value

iac.code: Monitor LastRotatedDate and the credential target in the secret owner rotation declaration; keep the 90-day schedule and application test runbook together.
iac.label: Review the secret owner lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect LastRotatedDate, current rotation configuration and the real credential target for this secret.
Have the credential and application owners repair or establish a tested rotation workflow, including consumer refresh and rollback.
Execute a reviewed real rotation and verify that it completes, clients authenticate and LastRotatedDate advances.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.rotated_within_90_.summary: A secret has no LastRotatedDate or the last completed rotation is more than 90 elapsed days old, failing the configured periodic rotation control.

caveats: A Lambda ARN by itself does not establish that rotation works; RotateSecret may start immediately and fail or disrupt clients if the function or target credential is not ready. Managed rotation mechanisms without a Lambda ARN still fail this exact predicate.

iac.code: Bind RotationRules and RotationLambdaARN to the owner-reviewed Lambda implementation for this secret ARN, including invocation rights and client rollover testing.
iac.label: Update the owning secret declaration

steps: Inspect the exact ARN, RotationRules and RotationLambdaARN and determine whether the credential supports Lambda-based rotation.
Have the application owner review the rotation function, network access, target credential permissions and a rollback path.
Configure a reviewed Lambda ARN and schedule, test a completed rotation and verify applications use the new credential.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.rotation_lambda.summary: A secret lacks either RotationRules or RotationLambdaARN, so the Lambda-based rotation configuration required by this check is incomplete.

caveats: RotationRules presence alone does not prove rotation is enabled or has succeeded; a managed external secret may require a different supported workflow. RotateSecret can start an immediate asynchronous rotation unless the owner explicitly chooses a tested schedule.

iac.code: Set RotationRules and a tested rotation Lambda for the exact ARN in the owner secret declaration; confirm permissions and client rollover before activation.
iac.label: Update the owning secret declaration

steps: Inspect the secret ARN, RotationRules, existing rotation method, application consumers and credential system of record.

aws.cb.secretsmanager.rotation_rules_pre.summary: A secret has no RotationRules metadata, so the automatic rotation schedule required by this check is absent.

caveats: An artificial GetSecretValue call would change an access signal without proving the application uses the secret. This check has no safe generic deletion command and does not establish that a never-accessed secret is disposable.

If it is needed, repair the legitimate consumer path and observe authentic access after the creation day; if not, retire it through a separate approved lifecycle change.
aws.cb.secretsmanager.used_after_creatio.summary: A secret was never accessed or LastAccessedDate is less than one calendar day after CreatedDate, so this source flags it as unused after creation.

caveats: This control applies even outside AWS Organizations; a portfolio with legitimate cross-account consumers may need a separately approved sharing design. The finding does not identify which consumers rely on the direct share, so no automatic deletion command is safe.
