caveats: The condition passes when any one failure role is present and does not prove every protocol logs failures. A role ARN alone does not prove trust, permissions or log delivery; configure each used protocol separately.

cli.label: Set an owner-reviewed protocol failure feedback role

iac.code: In topic Attributes, configure the actual ApplicationFailureFeedbackRoleArn, FirehoseFailureFeedbackRoleArn, HTTPFailureFeedbackRoleArn, LambdaFailureFeedbackRoleArn or SQSFailureFeedbackRoleArn for each used protocol, with reviewed role trust, CloudWatch Logs grants and retention. Test a delivery failure.
iac.label: Review the SNS owner declaration

steps: Inspect the topic attributes and list its active subscription protocols and owners.
Have the SNS and IAM owners choose the matching protocol failure-feedback role, verify sns.amazonaws.com trust and CloudWatch Logs permissions, then approve logging retention.
Set the reviewed protocol-specific FailureFeedbackRoleArn attribute and verify actual failed-delivery status logs.
aws.cb.sns.failure_feedback_role.summary: An SNS topic fails when none of its protocol-specific FailureFeedbackRoleArn attributes is set, leaving delivery-failure status without a configured feedback role.

caveats: This condition matches explicit sns:Publish only and does not match a wildcard action such as sns:*; it also skips any statement with a Condition block, even one that is ineffective. Review effective access separately.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove unconditioned wildcard Allow grants with explicit sns:Publish and replace them with scoped publisher permissions. Audit sns:* and ineffective Condition cases as a separate effective-access review.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the complete Policy for Allow wildcard-principal statements whose explicit Action includes sns:Publish.
Have the topic owner replace the grant with approved publisher principals and source conditions, preserving legitimate event producers.
Apply the reviewed Policy document and verify authorized publish calls and denial for an unapproved publisher.
aws.cb.sns.policy_no_public_publish.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Publish to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unrestricted publication.

caveats: The action matcher does not catch sns:* or a grant with any Condition block, even if that condition is weak. Changing subscription rights can interrupt new enrollments but does not remove existing subscriptions.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, scope explicit sns:Subscribe and sns:Receive Allow grants to approved principals and conditions. Separately inspect wildcard actions and current subscriptions; validate delivery after policy rollout.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect Policy Allow statements with wildcard principals and explicit sns:Subscribe or sns:Receive actions.
Have the topic owner identify approved subscriber identities and endpoint enrollment flow, then replace the unconditioned public grant.
Apply the reviewed Policy and verify expected subscriptions still work while an unapproved account cannot subscribe or receive.
aws.cb.sns.policy_no_public_subscribe.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Subscribe or sns:Receive to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unreviewed consumers.

caveats: An absent readable Policy passes this condition. The restriction parser recognizes only selected condition forms; arbitrary Condition text is not proof of constrained access. Policy replacement can break existing fanout.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove unrestricted wildcard Allow statements or bind them to approved principals and recognized source-account, source-ARN or organization conditions. Preserve tested service integration grants and audit publication and subscription results.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect all Allow statements with wildcard principals, their actions and the exact Condition operators and keys.
Have the topic policy owner replace unrestricted grants with reviewed principals or restrictive source-account, source-ARN or organization conditions for the real publishers and subscribers.
Apply the complete reviewed topic Policy and verify authorized publication and subscription alongside denied unauthorized callers.
aws.cb.sns.policy_no_unrestricted_wildca.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy contains an Allow wildcard-principal statement without a recognized restricting condition.

caveats: A topic with no readable Policy is not applicable here, unlike the similar strict topic control. A condition must actually constrain the caller; simply adding any condition is insufficient.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, express publisher and subscriber access with reviewed principals and effective restrictive conditions. Retain authorized fanout, test external denial and document any approved perimeter exception.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the topic Policy and enumerate public-facing Allow statements, including condition keys and actual caller context.
Have the security and topic owners approve explicit principals or a supported restrictive source or organization condition that preserves required integrations.
Apply the reviewed replacement Policy and verify the perimeter behavior and expected delivery paths.
aws.cb.sns.policy_prohibit_public_access.summary: An SNS topic fails the perimeter condition when its Policy allows a wildcard principal without an effective recognized restriction.

caveats: PendingConfirmation subscriptions are not applicable to this condition. Creating an HTTPS subscription alone does not clear the old HTTP finding; removing the old one before delivery verification can lose notifications.

cli.label: Create a reviewed HTTPS replacement subscription

iac.code: Replace Protocol=http with a confirmed HTTPS subscription in the topic owner declaration. Track SubscriptionArn identities, endpoint certificate validation and message delivery; retire the old subscription only after tested cutover.
iac.label: Review the SNS owner declaration

steps: Inspect the subscription attributes, endpoint owner and any pending confirmation state; confirm whether an HTTPS endpoint is available.
Have the endpoint owner provision HTTPS with a trusted certificate, create a parallel subscription and confirm it without embedding secrets in the URL.
Verify delivery and deduplication on HTTPS, then have the subscription owner remove the old HTTP subscription through a separately reviewed cutover.
aws.cb.sns.subscription_not_http.summary: A confirmed SNS subscription fails when its Protocol is plain http, exposing notification delivery to transport interception.

caveats: The source loop can return passing early when it encounters a restrictive SourceArn statement, even if a later statement is public. Do not add a benign statement to mask a public grant; review the whole policy.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove actual public grants and preserve only reviewed principal and restrictive-condition combinations. Inspect all statements independently because a restrictive SourceArn statement can mask later exposure in this control.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect every wildcard-principal Allow statement and its SourceArn, source-account, organization or endpoint conditions, not merely the first match.
Have the policy owner design a complete replacement with approved publisher and subscriber principals and restrictive conditions matching their real call paths.
Apply the reviewed replacement Policy and test access for authorized and unauthorized callers; reassess all statements manually.
aws.cb.sns.topic_not_publicly_accessible.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy exposes a wildcard principal through an Allow statement that the source does not consider restricted.

caveats: The condition compares a literal alias and does not independently prove key ownership for every other identifier. Existing messages may remain encrypted under their previous key, and lost KMS grants can interrupt producers or consumers.

cli.label: Inspect queue attributes and owner configuration
Apply only a reviewed KmsMasterKeyId attribute document

iac.code: Set Attributes.Attributes.KmsMasterKeyId in the queue owner declaration to the reviewed customer managed KMS key, preserving its old-key decrypt grants through message retention. Test producer and consumer paths after the update.
iac.label: Review the queue owner declaration

steps: Inspect KmsMasterKeyId and resolve any alias to the actual key ARN, then review its policy and queue producer and consumer grants.
Have the KMS and queue owners select an approved customer managed key and plan the key switch, rollback and expected KMS request cost.
Apply only the reviewed KmsMasterKeyId attribute and verify new message production, consumption and decrypt access.
aws.cb.sqs.cmk_encryption.summary: An SQS queue fails when KmsMasterKeyId is missing or equals the literal alias/aws/sqs, so the configured key is not a selected customer key.

caveats: The check only detects a nonempty RedrivePolicy string; it does not validate the target queue, maxReceiveCount, replay process or actual delivery. Lower retry counts can move messages before transient failures recover.

cli.label: Inspect queue attributes and owner configuration
Apply only a reviewed RedrivePolicy attribute document

iac.code: Set Attributes.Attributes.RedrivePolicy in the queue owner declaration using an approved dead-letter queue ARN and maxReceiveCount. Review queue type, redrive permissions and replay ownership before publishing; verify a controlled failed delivery.
iac.label: Review the queue owner declaration

steps: Inspect the source queue attributes, retry pattern and poison-message handling requirements.
Have the queue owner select an authorized dead-letter queue of the same standard or FIFO type, approve maxReceiveCount and review its redrive allow policy.
Apply only the reviewed RedrivePolicy attribute, then test a failing message and verify it reaches the dead-letter queue without disrupting normal consumers.
aws.cb.sqs.dead_letter_queue.summary: An SQS queue fails when its RedrivePolicy attribute is absent or empty, so failed deliveries lack a configured dead-letter destination.

caveats: This condition ignores policy conditions and therefore can flag an account-scoped wildcard grant that another policy check accepts. Do not remove a queue consumer grant without the owner and dependent service review.

cli.label: Inspect the complete existing queue policy
Apply a separately owner-reviewed queue Policy attribute

iac.code: In Attributes.Attributes.Policy, replace each Allow wildcard Principal with owner-approved scoped principal grants and preserve required service conditions. Review every producer and consumer path before publishing the complete queue Policy attribute.
iac.label: Review the queue policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect every queue Policy statement with Effect=Allow and a wildcard principal, including its actions, resources and conditions.
Have the policy owner replace each wildcard principal with reviewed specific principals or redesign the grant while preserving intended producer and consumer access.
Apply a separately reviewed Policy attribute document, verify access with authorized callers and rerun this exact condition.
aws.cb.sqs.policy_no_wildcard_allow.summary: An SQS queue fails when its Policy has any Allow statement with a wildcard principal, even if that statement has a restricting Condition.

caveats: An absent Policy is not applicable to this condition. The condition parser recognizes only specific restricting keys and operators; an arbitrary Condition is not proof of effective restriction. A policy replacement can interrupt integrations.

cli.label: Inspect the complete existing queue policy
Apply a separately owner-reviewed queue Policy attribute

iac.code: In Attributes.Attributes.Policy, review wildcard Allow grants against the supported account/source/network Condition keys and replace public grants with scoped, tested statements. Preserve authorized service principals and verify the perimeter after deployment.
iac.label: Review the queue policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the queue Policy, especially Allow statements with Principal=* and the existing Condition operators and keys.
Have the policy owner use explicit principals or a reviewed restrictive account, source or network condition that matches the actual caller path.
Apply a reviewed Policy attribute document and validate both intended access and public-access behavior.
aws.cb.sqs.policy_prohibit_public_access.summary: An SQS queue fails when its Policy has an Allow wildcard principal without a recognized restricting condition, exposing the queue under the perimeter rule.

cli.label: Inspect the complete existing queue policy
Apply a separately owner-reviewed queue Policy attribute

iac.label: Review the queue policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the queue Policy and identify wildcard Allow statements, their Condition blocks and the actual producer and consumer identities.

Apply the complete reviewed Policy attribute and verify authorized message flows and denied unauthorized paths.
aws.cb.sqs.queue_not_public_prowler.summary: An SQS queue fails when its Policy has a public Allow wildcard principal whose Condition does not restrict access to an approved caller context.

caveats: The native check treats every other account as untrusted because it has no external allowlist; a legitimate cross-account share needs explicit policy review, not silent deletion. Removing a grant may interrupt dependent Automation.

steps: Inspect the document Share permissions and identify each public or cross-account consumer, including production Automation dependencies.

Remove only the reviewed public or account grant, verify the remaining AccountIds and confirm authorized Automation consumers still work.
aws.cb.ssm.document_shared_only_with_tru.summary: An SSM document fails when Permissions.AccountIds contains all or any account other than the audited account, exposing its content beyond that account.

caveats: An instance with no Association items is not applicable. Empty Status counts as noncompliant for this exact check; no universal safe mutation can repair arbitrary association documents or target-side failures.

cli.label: Inspect every compliance item for the managed instance

Have the State Manager and workload owners repair the specific association document, parameters, IAM permission or target prerequisite that failed.
Run the association through its approved maintenance process and verify every Association item returns COMPLIANT.
aws.cb.ssm.instance_association_complian.summary: A managed instance fails when any Association compliance item has Status other than COMPLIANT, including an empty status value.

caveats: An instance without Patch items, or with only empty Patch statuses, is not applicable under this condition. Patching may require reboot and application testing; no universal safe install command applies across operating systems and baselines.

cli.label: Inspect every compliance item for the managed instance
Inspect patch state for the instance

iac.code: Declare RoleName AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal.AWS and attached ReadOnlyAccess disposition in a complete owner-approved trust model, including documented cross-account exceptions.
iac.label: Review IAM prowler role readonly not cross account declaration

steps: Inspect RoleName, exact ReadOnlyAccess attachment and the complete trust policy for every allowed AWS principal.
Have the account owners decide which cross-account readers are formally authorized and prepare a full replacement trust policy or alternate access design.
Apply the owner-reviewed trust change, test approved readers and verify the Prowler-style condition on the exact role.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_role_readonly_n.summary: A non-service role with ReadOnlyAccess policy name has a wildcard or another-account trust Principal.AWS.

caveats: Plain unconditioned service trust is not applicable to this specific check and is handled by the separate confused-deputy predicate; service-linked roles are excluded. An Allow NotAction statement is MANUAL. The helper does not replace a full IAM trust evaluation.

iac.code: Declare RoleName/Arn AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal, Action and Condition in a full owner-approved trust document with fixed source bounds, service compatibility tests and rollback.
iac.label: Review IAM role trust prowler role service trust bound to account declaration

steps: Inspect every service-principal trust Allow, its existing Condition operators and values, and the AWS resource actually invoking the role.
Have the resource and IAM owners replace unrelated conditions with an account-bounded aws:SourceAccount or service-supported aws:SourceArn/SourceOrgID restriction in a complete trust document.
Apply the owner-reviewed trust policy, test legitimate service calls and verify the account-bound condition on each in-scope statement.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_role_service_tr.summary: A conditioned service-principal trust statement lacks a fixed source account, source ARN account or organization boundary.

caveats: This check is commercial-partition only and ignores root without a password or active key. Any virtual device whose User.Arn contains root fails even if hardware MFA is also enrolled; never remove the current factor before testing the replacement.

iac.code: Declare root iam_account_summary.SummaryMap.AccountMFAEnabled and iam_virtual_mfa_device.User.Arn custody alongside a tested hardware MFA enrollment and break-glass recovery procedure.
iac.label: Review IAM prowler root hardware mfa declaration

steps: Inspect the root credential-report row, AccountMFAEnabled and virtual MFA device assignments without exposing credential or MFA seed material.
Have the root credential custodians enroll and test an approved physical security key or hardware token, document recovery and verify it works before changing any existing factor.
After the hardware factor is verified, retire the root virtual device through the supervised root-console process and confirm the account summary and virtual-device inventory.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_root_hardware_m.summary: Commercial-partition root with credentials lacks account MFA or has a virtual MFA device assigned to root.

caveats: The native source classifies device type from SerialNumber shape, not FIDO attestation; a missing device also fails. A hardware device cannot be enrolled safely by a copied command without user presence and recovery controls.

iac.code: Declare UserName MFADevices.items[*].SerialNumber enrollment with approved physical factor custody, tested sign-in and recovery procedures.
iac.label: Review IAM prowler user hardware mfa declaration

steps: Inspect UserName and each MFA device SerialNumber and type without exposing seed material or enrollment challenges.
Have the identity and user owners register a tested physical security key or hardware token and establish recovery before replacing existing factors.
Verify the hardware sign-in, then retire virtual or SMS factors through supervised identity workflow and confirm the device list.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_user_hardware_m.summary: An IAM user has no MFA device or has a virtual or SMS-style SerialNumber among MFADevices.items.

caveats: The native admin matcher selects particular Resource/NotResource forms and does not prove all paths to administrator privileges absent. A principal without inline policies is not applicable, and replacing the document changes permissions immediately.

iac.code: Declare UserName UserPolicyList[*].PolicyName and full PolicyDocument.Statement Effect/Action/NotAction/Resource/NotResource/Condition under owner-reviewed replacement and rollback.
iac.label: Review user Prowler inline no admin declaration

steps: Inspect UserName and each UserPolicyList document, identifying the exact administrative Action and Resource/NotResource statement and every affected workflow.

Have IAM and application owners approve a complete replacement inline policy in a separate file, preserving unrelated grants and testing recovery access. Replace the full document with explicit operations and resources after each principal owner approves a recovery administrator path.
Apply the reviewed full inline policy document, test allowed and denied actions, and recheck the exact principal finding.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_user_inline_no_.summary: An IAM user inline policy contains an administrative Action * grant on the source-selected Resource or NotResource shape.

caveats: The source expands over a pinned CloudTrail action catalog and ignores policy Condition semantics; finding presence does not prove a trail changed. A principal without inline policies is not applicable, and replacing the document changes permissions immediately.

iac.code: Declare UserName UserPolicyList[*].PolicyName and full PolicyDocument.Statement Effect/Action/NotAction/Resource/NotResource/Condition under owner-reviewed replacement and rollback.

Apply the reviewed full inline policy document, test allowed and denied actions, and recheck the exact principal finding.
aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_user_inline_no_.summary: An IAM user inline policy grants every pinned CloudTrail action on Resource *.

aws.claude_a.iam.prowler_user_inline_no_.summary: An IAM user inline policy grants every pinned KMS action on Resource *.

aws.claude_a.iam.role_no_inline_policies.summary: This role has one or more entries in its inline policy list.

iac.code: Declare RoleName ownership and RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate evidence with scheduled-use and disaster-recovery exceptions; retire only through a dependency-reviewed change.

aws.claude_a.iam.role_used_within_60_day.summary: An IAM role has no recorded RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate or its last use is at least 60 days old at the captured date.

caveats: Only root with a console password is in scope; the flags do not prove the quality or phishing resistance of the device. Root MFA enrollment requires root sign-in and device possession; no device secret or activation code belongs in copied CLI.

Move intended access to purpose-specific groups and retire default-group rules after owner and client impact review.
Recollect the security group and its dependencies, rerun this exact check and verify intended traffic separately.
aws.claude_a.vpc.default_sg_no_rules.summary: A default security group must have empty ingress and egress rule sets; any rule in either direction fails regardless of current use.

caveats: This setting governs new connection requests and does not retroactively revoke existing accepted connections. AWS-owned services are not applicable. Switching to manual acceptance can delay legitimate consumer onboarding.

iac.code: Declare account-owned ServiceId with AcceptanceRequired=true and a documented endpoint consumer approval workflow, preserving legitimate existing connections.
iac.label: Review VPC endpoint service acceptance required declaration

steps: Inspect ServiceId, Owner, AcceptanceRequired, current allowed principals and pending or accepted endpoint connections.
Have the service and consumer owners establish an approval process and review the impact on future consumer connections.
Require connection acceptance on the exact service and verify its setting; approve future connection requests only after consumer review.
aws.claude_a.vpc.endpoint_service_accept.summary: An account-owned VPC endpoint service has AcceptanceRequired=false.

caveats: The native rule treats every nonlocal principal as untrusted because no trusted-account allowlist is configured; it cannot decide business authorization. Removing permission prevents new connections and may affect established consumers; review them before change.

iac.code: Declare ServiceId AllowedPrincipals as an owner-approved trust list, and document any authorized cross-account exception rather than deleting it solely to satisfy this predicate.
iac.label: Review VPC endpoint service principals trusted declaration

steps: Inspect the exact ServiceId permissions and current endpoint consumers; map every AllowedPrincipals ARN to its owner and business purpose.
Have the service and consumer owners decide which cross-account principals should remain and prepare a reviewed removal set, preserving approved connections and future onboarding.
Remove only reviewed untrusted principals and verify the remaining list and consumer connectivity.
aws.claude_a.vpc.endpoint_service_princi.summary: An account-owned VPC endpoint service AllowedPrincipals list includes a wildcard or another account.

caveats: This check skips VPCs owned by another account; it fails if any associated log is not ACTIVE even when another is healthy. A newly created log does not repair an existing failed one.

iac.code: Declare VpcId-level FlowLogId, ResourceId, destination, TrafficType, retention and delivery role; verify FlowLogStatus=ACTIVE operationally.
iac.label: Review VPC flow logs active declaration

steps: Inspect the VpcId and all associated FlowLogId, ResourceId and FlowLogStatus values, including FAILED delivery and ownership.
Have the network and logging owners choose traffic type, CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination, retention, KMS access, IAM delivery role and expected cost.
Create a reviewed VPC flow log if absent; repair a failed destination or delivery role and verify every VPC flow log becomes ACTIVE.
aws.claude_a.vpc.flow_logs_active.summary: An account-owned VPC has no flow log or at least one of its FlowLogStatus values is not ACTIVE.

caveats: The source only fails an Allow whose normalized Action list is exactly [*], with wildcard principal and no Condition. Other broad forms may pass, and a condition key alone is not proof of effective restriction. Updating the endpoint policy replaces the complete document and can disrupt authorized traffic.

iac.code: Declare VpcEndpointId PolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal, Action, Resource and Condition as a full owner-approved policy scoped to actual endpoint callers; preserve required access.
iac.label: Review gateway endpoint access policy

steps: Inspect VpcEndpointId, VpcEndpointType and the complete PolicyDocument, identifying exact Allow statements and legitimate S3 or DynamoDB callers.
Have the network, storage and application owners approve narrower principals, actions, resource ARNs or fixed conditions while preserving required cross-account workflows.
Apply the complete reviewed replacement policy and test allowed and denied endpoint requests before removing fallback access.
aws.claude_a.vpc.gateway_endpoint_policy.summary: A Gateway endpoint policy has an unconditional Allow with wildcard Principal and Action exactly *.

caveats: The source only checks whether any attachment exists; it does not verify an authorized VPC. Attaching a gateway enables a possible internet path only when routes and controls allow it, and should not be done merely to clear an unused-resource finding.

iac.code: Declare InternetGatewayId ownership and an approved Attachments[*].VpcId only for VPCs needing an internet path; decommission unused gateways through owner-managed IaC.
iac.label: Review VPC igw attached declaration

steps: Inspect InternetGatewayId, attachments, tags, intended VPC and any IaC or change record reserving the gateway.
Have the network owner decide whether the detached gateway is a staged dependency, should be attached to an approved VPC or should be retired.
If approved for active internet access, attach it to the reviewed VPC and verify routes and security controls; otherwise retire through the managed configuration after dependency review.
aws.claude_a.vpc.igw_attached.summary: An Internet Gateway InternetGatewayId has an empty Attachments list.

caveats: The check skips subnets without network interfaces. Existing public addresses and launch-template interface settings need separate review. Disabling the default can break bootstrap or connectivity for workloads that rely on a public address.

iac.code: Declare SubnetId with MapPublicIpOnLaunch=false, plus explicit approved connectivity paths for private workloads and separate remediation for existing interfaces.
iac.label: Review VPC in use subnet no auto public ip declaration

steps: Inspect SubnetId, MapPublicIpOnLaunch, current public IPs, launch templates and applications requiring inbound reachability.
Have the network and service owners arrange private endpoints, load balancers or other approved access paths before changing the launch default.
Disable automatic public IPv4 assignment and verify the subnet attribute; review existing public interfaces separately.
aws.claude_a.vpc.in_use_subnet_no_auto_p.summary: An in-use subnet has MapPublicIpOnLaunch=true and can auto-assign public IPv4 to new instances.

caveats: This source accepts any endpoint with an ec2 substring in ServiceName regardless of endpoint state or type; the operation should target the exact regional EC2 interface service. A VPC without network interfaces is not applicable. Endpoint hourly/data charges and DNS changes need review.

iac.code: Declare VpcId endpoint with exact regional com.amazonaws.<REGION>.ec2 ServiceName, Interface type, private DNS, owner-approved subnet and security group choices; verify status and callers separately.
iac.label: Review VPC in use vpc ec2 endpoint declaration

steps: Inspect the VpcId, network interfaces, endpoints, routes and EC2 API callers that currently use public paths.
Have network and application owners choose an EC2 interface endpoint, private DNS, at least two suitable subnets, endpoint security groups and access policy.
Create the reviewed endpoint, verify its ServiceName and DNS resolution, and test authorized EC2 API calls over the private path.
aws.claude_a.vpc.in_use_vpc_ec2_endpoint.summary: A VPC with network interfaces has no endpoint whose ServiceName contains ec2.

caveats: This in-use check accepts a flow-log record regardless of FlowLogStatus; failed delivery still needs operational repair. A VPC without network interfaces is not applicable.

iac.code: Declare VpcId-level FlowLogId, ResourceId, destination, TrafficType, retention and delivery role; verify FlowLogStatus=ACTIVE operationally.
iac.label: Review VPC in use vpc has flow log declaration

steps: Inspect the VpcId, joined network interfaces and any flow-log ResourceId values before choosing the logging destination.
Have the network and logging owners approve traffic type, destination, retention, KMS and delivery role for that used VPC.
Create the reviewed VPC flow log and inspect its delivery status and records after activation.
aws.claude_a.vpc.in_use_vpc_has_flow_log.summary: A VPC containing a network interface has no flow-log record whose ResourceId equals its VpcId.

caveats: This source only counts 0.0.0.0/0 routes to igw- in explicit/main route tables; it does not inspect IPv6, public IP assignment or ingress controls. A VPC without ENIs is not applicable. Route changes can interrupt running applications; subnet count and routing classification alone do not prove isolation.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnet tiers with explicit route_table.Associations and Routes.DestinationCidrBlock/GatewayId or NatGatewayId aligned to owner-approved public and private workloads; verify actual ingress and egress.
iac.label: Review VPC in use vpc public and private subnets declaration

references.title: Official VPC public and private subnet example

steps: Inspect VpcId, all subnet associations and effective main or explicit route tables; map existing public listeners and internal workloads.
Have network and service owners design distinct subnet tiers, ingress paths, private egress through NAT/endpoints, CIDRs, security controls and workload placement.
Create or migrate to owner-approved subnet and route declarations, verify route paths and application connectivity from both tiers.
aws.claude_a.vpc.in_use_vpc_public_and_p.summary: An in-use VPC lacks both an IGW-routed public subnet and a non-IGW-routed private subnet.

caveats: The check skips VPCs without network interfaces; multiple subnet zones alone do not prove the deployed service uses more than one zone. AZ-specific capacity and cross-zone traffic may add cost.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnets with distinct AvailabilityZone values and separate owner-approved CIDRs; map workload replicas and failover to both zones.

references.title: Official VPC subnets in Availability Zones

Have the network and application owners approve a second zone, subnet CIDR, routes, security controls, service support and capacity; plan workload migration or redundant placement.
Create the reviewed second-zone subnet and deploy or migrate workload capacity into it, then verify both zones in inventory and service health.
aws.claude_a.vpc.in_use_vpc_subnets_mult.summary: A VPC with network interfaces has subnets in at most one distinct AvailabilityZone.

caveats: The source joins by GroupName rather than GroupId, so same-name groups in different VPCs can produce a false match; verify exact ENI group IDs before changing anything. Non-launch-wizard groups are not applicable.

iac.code: Declare GroupId and GroupName replacement with narrow application permissions, and map network_interface.Groups[*].GroupName and IDs to exact owning services before migration.
iac.label: Review security group launch wizard sg not attached declaration

steps: Inspect the launch-wizard GroupName, exact GroupId, all matching ENI group names and the workloads behind those interfaces.
Have service and network owners define a purpose-built security group with only the application-required ingress and egress rules, including management access.
Migrate each reviewed ENI or its owning service to the replacement group, validate connectivity, and separately retire the launch-wizard group if no references remain.
aws.claude_a.vpc.launch_wizard_sg_not_at.summary: A security group whose GroupName starts with launch-wizard is matched by name to an ENI group.

caveats: An empty association list does not prove that deleting the ACL is safe; no deletion command is provided.

cli.label: Inspect the operator-identified network ACL and ordered entries

iac.code: Inspect Entries.RuleNumber, Egress, RuleAction, Protocol, PortRange, CidrBlock and Ipv6CidrBlock plus Associations in the owner-managed ACL. Associate the ACL with an owner-approved subnet if intended, or plan retirement only after a complete dependency review. Preserve a rollback and verify subnet traffic.
iac.label: Review the network ACL owner declaration

steps: Inspect the ACL Associations list and confirm subnet and VPC ownership.
Associate the ACL with an owner-approved subnet if intended, or plan retirement only after a complete dependency review.
Recollect the network ACL, rerun this exact check and test intended subnet traffic in both directions.
aws.claude_a.vpc.nacl_associated.summary: Network ACL Associations must contain at least one entry; an empty list fails even for a default ACL.

caveats: No single safe CLI mutation is provided: rule number, direction, CIDR and subnet consumers must be reviewed. All collected network ACLs are in scope; there is no non-default-security-group prerequisite.

cli.label: Inspect the operator-identified network ACL and ordered entries

iac.code: Inspect Entries.RuleNumber, Egress, RuleAction, Protocol, PortRange, CidrBlock and Ipv6CidrBlock plus Associations in the owner-managed ACL. Have the subnet owner design a lower-numbered deny or a narrower replacement allow, test both address families, then change only the approved entry. Preserve a rollback and verify subnet traffic.
iac.label: Review the network ACL owner declaration

steps: Inspect IPv4 and IPv6 ingress entries in rule-number order, their actions and associated subnets.
Have the subnet owner design a lower-numbered deny or a narrower replacement allow, test both address families, then change only the approved entry.
Recollect the network ACL, rerun this exact check and test intended subnet traffic in both directions.
aws.claude_a.vpc.nacl_no_world_all_ports.summary: ordered network ACL ingress must not first allow all protocols from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

caveats: This check flags matching Allow entries even when an earlier Deny would block traffic; no universal mutation is safe without rule-number, subnet and client review.

cli.label: Inspect the operator-identified network ACL and ordered entries

iac.code: Inspect Entries.RuleNumber, Egress, RuleAction, Protocol, PortRange, CidrBlock and Ipv6CidrBlock plus Associations in the owner-managed ACL. Replace broad Allow entries with owner-approved administrative CIDRs or lower-numbered Deny entries after testing access and ACL order. Preserve a rollback and verify subnet traffic.
iac.label: Review the network ACL owner declaration

steps: Inspect every ingress Allow entry for 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 and a port range containing 22 or 3389.
Replace broad Allow entries with owner-approved administrative CIDRs or lower-numbered Deny entries after testing access and ACL order.
Recollect the network ACL, rerun this exact check and test intended subnet traffic in both directions.
aws.claude_a.vpc.nacl_no_world_remote_ad.summary: Network ACL must contain no ingress Allow entry from a world CIDR covering port 22 or 3389, or all traffic; TCP and UDP entries are checked.

caveats: No single safe CLI mutation is offered because rule order, number and approved admin CIDRs are not finding evidence. All collected ACLs are in scope.

aws.claude_a.vpc.nacl_no_world_tcp_3389.summary: ordered ACL ingress must not first allow TCP 3389 from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

aws.claude_a.vpc.nondefault_nacl_associa.summary: A non-default network ACL must have at least one association with a SubnetId; no matching subnet association fails.

caveats: This branch ignores default VPCs and is not applicable when the account has no VPCs. A second empty VPC is not a disaster-recovery capability; workloads, data, replication, DNS and failover need independent review.

cli.label: Inspect VPCs in each approved Region

iac.code: Declare AccountId-approved VpcId resources in two required Region values with IsDefault=false, plus workload/data replication, routing, DNS and failover evidence; avoid an empty compliance-only VPC.
iac.label: Review second-Region VPC and recovery design

steps: Inspect the complete enabled-Region VPC inventory, owner account IDs, IsDefault flags, workload dependencies and actual recovery objectives.
Have application, data and network owners design a second-Region landing zone, addressing, connectivity, replication, recovery tests and cost based on the service continuity requirement.
Deploy the reviewed regional infrastructure and workload/data recovery path, test failover, and verify VpcId records in two Regions with IsDefault=false.
aws.claude_a.vpc.nondefault_vpcs_in_mult.summary: An account with VPCs has non-default VpcId records in zero or one Region.

caveats: This branch excludes CreateRouteTable-origin routes and does not compare the accepter CIDR; it scans route tables containing the connection. Its narrower source can pass other broad peering routes. A whole-VPC CIDR may be intentional for approved connectivity, and removing it blindly can disconnect applications; no generic route mutation is offered.

Have both VPC owners approve only the subnet prefixes and application paths needed across peering, including return routes and security groups.
Replace each reviewed overbroad route through managed network change, validate reachability and recheck the exact route-table destinations.
aws.claude_a.vpc.peering_route_tables_le.summary: A peering route table has a non-main-origin route to 0.0.0.0/0 or the requester VPC CIDR.

caveats: This branch normalizes and compares both requester and accepter primary CIDRs, and joins only routes whose VpcPeeringConnectionId matches the connection. steps: Inspect the peering connection CIDRs, every route table referencing its VpcPeeringConnectionId and the exact broad DestinationCidrBlock entries.

Have both network owners decide whether a pending/inactive connection is needed and whether a cross-account link is explicitly authorized under the trust model.
Complete or retire the owner-approved connection and adjust route and security group access through a separate reviewed change; verify Status.Code and both OwnerId values.
aws.claude_a.vpc.peering_same_account_ac.summary: A VPC peering connection is not active or its requester and accepter OwnerId values differ.

caveats: The native classification calls a default route to either igw- or nat- public, although NAT normally provides outbound-only access; classify actual ingress separately. An empty VPC fails, and a token pair of subnets is not workload segmentation. Route changes can interrupt running applications; subnet count and routing classification alone do not prove isolation.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnet tiers with explicit route_table.Associations and Routes.DestinationCidrBlock/GatewayId or NatGatewayId aligned to owner-approved public and private workloads; verify actual ingress and egress.

Have the network and service owners decide whether the group is reserved for a planned deployment, can be reused, or should be retired after dependency review.

aws.claude_a.vpc.sg_attached_to_eni.summary: A security group GroupId has no matching network_interface.Groups.GroupId in collected ENIs.

caveats: The extra instance association broadens the join but still cannot prove a group is unused by future launch templates or deployments. Deleting it blindly can break a later scale-out or recovery event.

iac.code: Declare GroupId ownership, current network_interface.Groups and instance.SecurityGroups references, and any future launch-template dependencies; retire only after explicit service approval.

Remove only an owner-reviewed world-CIDR rule ID

Consolidate reviewed rules with prefix lists or referenced groups, validate equivalent access, and stage changes without crossing service quotas. Preserve a tested rollback path.

Consolidate reviewed rules with prefix lists or referenced groups, validate equivalent access, and stage changes without crossing service quotas.
Recollect the security group and its dependencies, rerun this exact check and verify intended traffic separately.

caveats: The source checks both FromPort and ToPort for IPv4 world ingress, so an 80-to-65535 range fails. IPv6 is outside this predicate. Public HTTP/HTTPS also requires application-layer controls; there is no safe generic revoke command without the exact rule and owner.

Have the service and network owners approve the exact public listener ports and replacement private ingress sources; preserve required administration access through an approved path.
Apply an owner-reviewed rule change to the exact offending permission, validate service access and scan all overlapping ranges and IPv6 rules separately.
aws.claude_a.vpc.sg_world_v4_only_80_443.summary: An IPv4 world ingress rule has a missing port, a port outside 80 or 443, or a range whose ToPort differs from FromPort.

caveats: This setting affects future launches; it does not remove public addresses already allocated to running interfaces. Disabling the default can break bootstrap or connectivity for workloads that rely on a public address.

steps: Inspect SubnetId, MapPublicIpOnLaunch, current public IPs, launch templates and applications requiring inbound reachability.
Have the network and service owners arrange private endpoints, load balancers or other approved access paths before changing the launch default.
Disable automatic public IPv4 assignment and verify the subnet attribute; review existing public interfaces separately.
aws.claude_a.vpc.subnet_no_auto_public_i.summary: Subnet MapPublicIpOnLaunch is true, so new instances can receive a public IPv4 address by default.

caveats: The check covers every VPC, including an empty or intentionally single-zone VPC; a second empty subnet alone does not make workloads resilient. AZ-specific capacity and cross-zone traffic may add cost.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnets with distinct AvailabilityZone values and separate owner-approved CIDRs; map workload replicas and failover to both zones.

steps: Inspect the VpcId, existing subnet AvailabilityZone values, CIDR capacity and deployed workload placement.
Have the network and application owners approve a second zone, subnet CIDR, routes, security controls, service support and capacity; plan workload migration or redundant placement.
Create the reviewed second-zone subnet and deploy or migrate workload capacity into it, then verify both zones in inventory and service health.

caveats: The check does not establish that an empty VPC is unsafe. Creating a token subnet in an unused VPC adds cost/management burden and is not an appropriate response.

iac.code: If the VpcId is retained for workloads, declare a subnet with owner-approved CIDR, Availability Zone, route table and network controls; otherwise remove it through a dependency-reviewed retirement plan.

steps: Inspect the VPC purpose, CIDR allocation, routes, dependencies and whether it is intentionally empty or being decommissioned.
Have the network owner either approve an appropriate subnet CIDR and Availability Zone for a needed VPC or decommission the unused VPC through a separate dependency-reviewed plan.
Create the approved subnet only when workloads need it, then verify its VpcId and effective route-table association.
aws.claude_a.vpc.vpc_has_subnets.summary: A VPC VpcId has no matching subnet.VpcId in the collected subnet inventory.

caveats: The source counts VPC records across collected Regions and fails empty inventory; it does not prove workloads or data are resilient. Inventory must cover all enabled Regions; a token empty VPC in another Region would satisfy the count without useful recovery.

cli.label: Inspect VPCs in each approved Region

iac.code: Declare AccountId-approved VpcId resources in two required Region values, plus workload/data replication, routing, DNS and failover evidence; avoid an empty compliance-only VPC.
iac.label: Review second-Region VPC and recovery design

steps: Inspect the complete enabled-Region VPC inventory, owner account IDs, workload dependencies and actual recovery objectives.
Have application, data and network owners design a second-Region landing zone, addressing, connectivity, replication, recovery tests and cost based on the service continuity requirement.
Deploy the reviewed regional infrastructure and workload/data recovery path, test failover, and verify VpcId records in two Regions.
aws.claude_a.vpc.vpcs_in_multiple_region.summary: An account VPC inventory has VpcId records in zero or one Region.

caveats: This is operational tunnel state, not proof of application reachability. Unexpected telemetry shape yields UNKNOWN; an AWS-side tunnel option change can cause replacement and traffic interruption, so no blind modify command is offered.

iac.code: Declare VpnConnectionId with two independently configured customer gateway tunnel peers and monitored VgwTelemetry[*].Status=UP; keep pre-shared key handling in the approved secret system.
iac.label: Review VPN vpn both tunnels up declaration

steps: Inspect VpnConnectionId, both tunnel OutsideIpAddress and Status values, CloudWatch metrics, BGP status and customer gateway device logs.
Have the network and customer-gateway owners investigate IKE proposals, pre-shared key storage, route advertisements, firewall reachability and maintenance events without exposing key material.
Repair the specific DOWN tunnel with the customer gateway owner, fail over traffic safely and verify both telemetry entries become UP.
aws.claude_a.vpc.vpn_both_tunnels_up.summary: A Site-to-Site VPN connection has exactly two VgwTelemetry records but fewer than two have Status=UP.

caveats: The native check passes when only one tunnel logs, so it does not prove both are covered. ModifyVpnTunnelOptions changes one tunnel at a time and may replace or interrupt it; the full reviewed request must preserve IKE and pre-shared-key settings without exposing secrets in this template.

iac.code: Declare VpnConnectionId TunnelOptions[*].LogOptions.CloudWatchLogOptions.LogEnabled=true for each approved tunnel with encrypted CloudWatch destination, retention and documented maintenance impact.

steps: Inspect both tunnel logging flags, current outside IP addresses, tunnel options and the approved CloudWatch log group and access policy.
Have network and logging owners approve destination retention, KMS, data handling, cost and the possibility that tunnel-option changes replace a tunnel.
Apply a complete reviewed option document to one chosen tunnel during a maintenance window and verify its logging flag and log delivery; extend to the other tunnel for actual coverage.

caveats: MSK Serverless is NOT_APPLICABLE. Broker type matters: Standard and Express can have different supported targets. An older or incomparable target, an ambiguous/missing cluster-specific source row, or incomplete version inventory remains UNKNOWN, not a reason to upgrade.

A deprecated current version can fail even when no safe target is currently available; in that case use owner/AWS support review and do not run the update example. Version downgrades are unsupported, and this check does not establish client compatibility or unattended upgrade safety.

The --current-version argument is the MSK cluster Version concurrency token from DescribeClusterV2, not the Apache Kafka version string. A rolling upgrade can affect clients and availability; verify the returned operation and workload health.

cli.label: Inspect the exact MSK cluster and current-version token
Inspect update targets compatible with this cluster
Upgrade only to a reviewed, cluster-compatible ACTIVE target

iac.code: Set Provisioned.CurrentBrokerSoftwareInfo.KafkaVersion only to a cluster-specific compatible ACTIVE target after client and availability review; preserve the current cluster Version concurrency token for the update and monitor the rolling operation. Do not select the global ListKafkaVersions maximum.
iac.label: Review the owner-controlled MSK version declaration

references.title: Amazon MSK Apache Kafka version upgrade procedure
Amazon MSK version upgrade best practices

steps: Inspect the exact provisioned cluster ARN, broker type, current KafkaVersion, ListKafkaVersions status and its own GetCompatibleKafkaVersions SourceVersion row. A deprecated current version fails independently; an ACTIVE current version fails only for a provably newer ACTIVE target returned for this cluster.

If the current version is deprecated but no valid compatible target is returned, investigate with the streaming owner and AWS support rather than selecting a global version or fabricating an upgrade path. Treat missing, older, malformed or incomparable target evidence as UNKNOWN until corrected.

For an actual cluster-specific newer ACTIVE target, review client compatibility, broker availability, partition replication, quotas, configuration compatibility, maintenance window and rollback with the streaming owner. Obtain the current cluster Version concurrency token from DescribeClusterV2 immediately before any approved change.

Only after that review, upgrade to the specifically returned compatible target, monitor the rolling operation and client health, then recollect KafkaVersion and both version inventories. A passing result means no newer ACTIVE target was reported for this cluster, not the globally newest Kafka release.
aws.cb.kafka.latest_version.summary: Plan a supported MSK Kafka version upgrade for a deprecated broker version or an available newer compatible target.

caveats: This predicate checks the Aurora MySQL parameter values, not log generation, CloudWatch export, retention or comprehensive audit coverage. Unsupported event spelling or unknown parameter evidence is UNKNOWN, not a reason to overwrite settings.

AWS documents that these audit parameters do not require a cluster restart when the group is already attached, while first association does; other parameter/group changes may differ. A shared custom group affects every attached cluster, and QUERY events can increase volume and expose sensitive query text.

cli.label: Inspect the exact Aurora MySQL cluster and attached group
Inspect current cluster audit parameter values
Apply owner-reviewed audit parameters to the selected custom group

iac.code: For DBClusterArn with Engine=aurora-mysql, declare ClusterParameterGroupValues.server_audit_logging=ON and server_audit_events as one or more owner-approved uppercase comma-separated event names in a custom cluster parameter group; review shared consumers and delivery separately.
iac.label: Review Aurora MySQL audit parameter declaration

references.title: Aurora MySQL Advanced Auditing and supported events

steps: Inspect the exact Aurora MySQL DBClusterArn, its attached cluster parameter group, ClusterParameterGroupValues.server_audit_logging and server_audit_events. ON or 1 with a nonempty comma-separated list of supported uppercase events passes; OFF/0 or an empty event list fails, while missing or unrecognized facts stay UNKNOWN.

With the database and audit owners, select at least one supported event from CONNECT, QUERY, QUERY_DCL, QUERY_DDL, QUERY_DML and TABLE, with uppercase names and no spaces. Check existing include/exclude user settings, audit volume, retention and whether separate log delivery is required.

Change only the reviewed custom cluster parameter group values using the AWS-documented apply method; review every cluster sharing the group and whether first association requires a restart. Verify effective ON/1 and selected events, inspect a representative audit log, then recollect and rerun.
aws.cb.rds.aurora_mysql_server_audit_log.summary: Enable Aurora MySQL Advanced Auditing for reviewed event types in the flagged cluster parameter group.

caveats: This check reads allowlisted collected parameter strings only; it does not prove negotiated TLS, certificate validation, or every client path. Do not change parameters when engine, cluster association, MariaDB version or parameter values are unavailable or unrecognized.

Parameter groups can be shared. AWS documents different application behavior by engine and parameter; do not assume a universal reboot or no-reboot rule. Enforcing TLS can disconnect clients that cannot negotiate or validate the server certificate.

steps: Verify DBInstanceArn, Engine=mariadb and EngineVersion at least 10.5, then inspect ParameterGroupValues.require_secure_transport in the attached DB parameter group. ON or 1 passes, OFF or 0 fails, older MariaDB is NOT_APPLICABLE, and missing or unrecognized version/value is UNKNOWN.

Set require_secure_transport=ON in the reviewed custom DB parameter group with the supported apply method; AWS documents no instance reboot for this parameter update. Verify effective ON/1 and representative client access, then recollect and rerun.

aws.cb.rds.instance_iam_auth_all_engines.summary: Enable IAM database authentication only for the flagged supported standalone RDS MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL instance.
steps: Inspect the exact DBInstanceArn, Engine, EngineVersion, DBInstanceClass, DBClusterIdentifier, DBSubnetGroup.Subnets[].SubnetOutpost and IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled. Cluster members, known unsupported engines and RDS on Outposts are not instance-level remediation targets.

For a false instance flag, confirm the same Region and exact engine/version/class option has one nonconflicting SupportsIAMDatabaseAuthentication=true result. Missing, denied, empty or conflicting capability evidence remains UNKNOWN and must not trigger an update.

Review database-user prerequisites, rds-db:connect scope, TLS, application token refresh and connection pooling with database and identity owners. Schedule an approved modify-db-instance change; omit --apply-immediately unless its timing and dependency impact are separately approved.

Read back the instance flag after the maintenance window, test an authorized IAM database login and existing password clients, recollect matching capability and instance facts, then rerun aws.cb.rds.instance_iam_auth_all_engines.

iac.code: For only the source-confirmed supported standalone DB instance, declare IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled=true (or the IaC equivalent) with a separate least-privilege rds-db:connect policy and database-user migration plan; review the change and rollback.

caveats: The native evaluator passes an observed true instance flag as configuration evidence only; it does not prove any database user or client authenticates with IAM. A false flag fails only with matching regional engine/version/class SupportsIAMDatabaseAuthentication=true evidence.

Aurora and Multi-AZ DB cluster members use the cluster IAM-auth setting; known unsupported engines and RDS on Outposts are NOT_APPLICABLE. For a disabled instance flag, missing/denied/empty/conflicting capability or missing placement evidence is UNKNOWN; an observed true flag can pass as configuration evidence without capability or absent placement. Observed malformed placement and unrecognized engines remain UNKNOWN.

IAM DB auth uses short-lived tokens and extra instance memory. PostgreSQL IAM-auth users cannot also use password authentication and IAM cannot be combined with Kerberos there; test replication and connection pooling dependencies. Enabling the flag alone does not grant rds-db:connect or create a database user.

Without --apply-immediately RDS schedules the change for the next maintenance window; any immediate change needs separate availability and client-owner approval. No command is executed by the product.
